Adobe Workfront Enterprise work management for marketing and creative operations: projects, requests, proofing, timesheets and portfolio planning, sold by quote.
EnterpriseAdobe 2001 Very large QuoteNo free plan 70-120 3.2Mean of the six criteria: 3.2 out of 5

Adobe Workfront - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncTwo-way calendar sync: Not native.

Summary

Adobe Workfront runs projects, incoming requests, proofing and approvals, timesheets and portfolio planning in one tenant. It is bought by large marketing, creative and operations departments, often alongside Adobe’s Creative Cloud and Experience Cloud.

Work is organised as portfolios, programs, projects, tasks and issues, with Gantt charts that show predecessors and the critical path, Kanban and Scrum boards, calendar reports and a resource planner. Workfront Planning adds a separate record-based layer for campaign and strategy planning. Calendar sync is now missing: the legacy Home calendar’s Outlook link was removed in October 2024 and the Outlook add-in stopped working in October 2025.

There is no published price and no free plan. Adobe sells Workflow Select, Prime and Ultimate packages by quote, with Standard, Light and Contributor licences; strategic portfolio planning and environment promotion start at Prime, Data Connect and business rules at Ultimate, and Planning and Fusion are separate purchases.

Workfront falls under Adobe Experience Cloud’s SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scope, with data held in the US or in the EU (Ireland, the Netherlands, Germany) as set in the contract. AI Assistant requires a signed Adobe Gen AI agreement and is turning into CX Enterprise Coworker from September 2026. Leaving means row-capped report exports or the REST API.

Assessment

Value for money1.0
Every package and licence type is quote-only, with no free plan and automation through Fusion metered separately.
Ease of use2.0
Access levels, licence types, custom forms and templates need a trained administrator before a team is productive.
Enterprise features4.8
Adobe Admin Console identity, granular access levels, portfolios, programs, resource planning and Experience Cloud certifications.
Interface flexibility4.5
Gantt with critical path, boards, calendar reports, dashboards, custom forms, Fusion automation and a separate Planning product.
Data control4.0
SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 under Experience Cloud, US or EU hosting set at contract, but no self-managed edition.
Portability3.0
Report exports to Excel, CSV and TSV stop at 50,000 to 100,000 rows; the REST API is the realistic route out.

Record

First launched
2001. Release of @task, the product AtTask sold before renaming itself Workfront in 2015.
Vendor
Adobe Inc. Public company (NASDAQ: ADBE), headquartered in San Jose, California, US; Adobe bought Workfront of Lehi, Utah for $1.5 billion in December 2020.
Website
business.adobe.com/products/workfront.html
Plans
Workflow Select, Workflow Prime and Workflow Ultimate, plus Planning Select, Prime and Ultimate and Workfront Fusion automation, all quote-only; older customers may still hold the legacy Select, Prime and Ultimate packages.
Free plan
No free plan; Adobe offers demos, and a free 60-day Workfront Planning trial ran from 2 March to 1 May 2026 for existing Workflow customers.
Hosting
Adobe-run multi-tenant clusters in cloud providers’ data centres. Adobe’s Experience Cloud hosting-locations page (updated 5 November 2026) shows Workfront core processing and storage sites in Oregon, California, Iowa and Virginia in the US and in Ireland, the Netherlands and Germany in the EU, with the location provisioned at contract signing. No Asia-Pacific site, and no self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security
Covered by Adobe Experience Cloud’s SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27017 and ISO 27018 certifications and HIPAA-ready status; not FedRAMP. SSO and user provisioning through the Adobe Admin Console on every package; environment promotion needs Prime or Ultimate, and business rules and Data Connect need Workflow Ultimate. Customer-managed encryption keys are not documented.
Calendar sync
None current. The Outlook two-way sync on the legacy Home calendar went with Legacy Home in October 2024, and Workfront for Outlook stopped working when Microsoft disabled legacy Exchange tokens on 1 October 2025. No Google Calendar integration or iCal feed is documented.
Data out
Reports and lists export to PDF, Excel (.xls up to 65,000 rows, .xlsx up to 100,000), CSV and tab-delimited (50,000 rows); dashboards only to PDF. Full REST API; Data Connect warehouse access on Ultimate. Kick-Starts import and export via Excel.
Platforms
Web; Adobe Workfront apps for iOS and Android; Workfront View for iPad.
AI
AI Assistant on Select or higher with a Standard licence and a signed Adobe Gen AI agreement; it summarises work and writes formulas, and is being replaced by CX Enterprise Coworker from September 2026. AI Collaborators (agents assignable to tasks) became generally available in August 2026. Adobe says customer data is not used to train the Azure OpenAI models behind AI Assistant.
Integrations
Workfront Fusion, Adobe’s own integration platform, lists over 70 connectors (Adobe Experience Manager, Creative Cloud, Salesforce, Jira, Slack, Microsoft Teams among them) and is metered by operations; a full REST API and event subscriptions sit beside it, and an MCP server was added in 2026.
Market signal
More than 3,000 customers and one million users when Adobe agreed to buy it in November 2020 (KMWorld, 12 November 2020); now a product line of Adobe, a large public company.
Caveat
Prices are never published, and Adobe reorganised packaging into separate Workflow, Planning and Automation purchases, so quotes from older comparisons may not match what is sold in 2026.
Confidence
High

Asana Work management for teams: tasks and projects shown as lists, boards, calendars and timelines, with portfolios, goals and AI agents on top.
TeamsAsana 2011 Very large $10.99†Free plan 200-400 4.0Mean of the six criteria: 4.0 out of 5

Asana - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncOne-way only: an iCal subscription of a project or My Tasks, and an Outlook Calendar integration that pushes Asana changes to events but not back.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. One-way only: an iCal subscription of a project or My Tasks, and an Outlook Calendar integration that pushes Asana changes to events but not back.

Summary

Asana organises work as tasks inside projects, with the same task able to sit in several projects at once. It is sold to whole organisations that want one shared place for team plans, from marketing calendars to cross-functional launches.

Every project can be shown as a list, board, calendar, timeline or Gantt chart, and portfolios and goals roll projects up for managers. Rules, forms and custom fields handle routine workflow. Since 2025 Asana has added AI Teammates and AI Studio, which run agents and automations against a monthly allowance of requests and credits.

The free Personal plan was cut to two users in November 2025, so a team of three must pay from day one. Starter at $10.99 a seat adds timeline and automations; time tracking, approvals and advanced reporting sit on Advanced at $24.99. Above five users seats are bought in steps of 5, then 10 above 30 users, and AI use beyond the included 5 requests per user per month (up to 50 per account below Enterprise) is charged at $0.50 to $0.60 per request.

Asana holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certificates. Data residency in Europe, Australia or Japan, customer-managed encryption keys and audit logs come with Enterprise+, and Asana states that neither it nor its AI partners train models on customer data. Projects export to CSV or JSON, but the full organisation export is Enterprise+ only, so leaving a smaller plan means working through the API.

Assessment

Value for money2.8
Free for only two people since late 2025, then $10.99 a seat with timeline, and $24.99 for time tracking.
Ease of use4.2
Tasks, sections and My Tasks are quick to learn; portfolios, goals and rules take deliberate setup.
Enterprise features4.8
SAML and SCIM on Enterprise, audit logs, SIEM and residency on Enterprise+, admin console and ISO 27001 certification.
Interface flexibility4.3
List, board, calendar, timeline, Gantt, dashboards, portfolios, forms, rules and custom fields, mostly from Starter up.
Data control4.5
Data residency in Europe, Australia or Japan and customer-held keys through EKM, both on Enterprise+ only.
Portability3.4
Project CSV omits comments; a full organisation JSON export with attachments is reserved for Enterprise+ admins.

Record

First launched
2011. Public launch of the web app in November 2011; the company was founded in 2008.
Vendor
Asana, Inc. Publicly listed on the NYSE (ASAN); headquartered in San Francisco, United States.
Website
asana.com
Plans
Personal free (up to 2 users); Starter $10.99 annual or $13.49 monthly; Advanced $24.99 annual or $30.49 monthly; Enterprise and Enterprise+ by quote.
Free plan
Personal is free for 1 or 2 people with unlimited tasks and projects in list, board and calendar views; no timeline, automations, custom fields or dashboards.
Hosting
Asana-operated cloud, US by default; data residency in Europe, Australia or Japan on Enterprise+. No self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security
SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701, CSA STAR Level 1, HIPAA support. SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise; audit logs, SIEM integration and EKM on Enterprise+.
Calendar sync
One-way: iCal subscription links for a project or My Tasks (tasks need a due date), and an Outlook Calendar integration that sends Asana changes to Outlook but not back. Available on all plans.
Data out
Per-project CSV (no comments or attachments) and JSON export; a full organisation export as JSON, with optional attachments, only on Enterprise+ and legacy Enterprise. Public REST API with webhooks; CSV importer.
Platforms
Web, iOS, Android, desktop apps for macOS and Windows.
AI
Asana AI, AI Teammates and AI Studio on all paid plans with 5 requests per user per month (capped per account) and monthly AI Studio credits; extra requests are paid. Asana states it does not use customer data for training and contractually bars its AI partners from doing so.
Integrations
The app directory lists several hundred apps, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, Salesforce, Jira Cloud, GitHub, Zoom, Power BI, Zapier and Claude; a public REST API with webhooks is documented at developers.asana.com.
Market signal
Asana reported revenue of $790.8 million for fiscal 2026 (year to 31 January 2026), with 25,928 customers spending $5,000 or more a year, per its results release of 2 March 2026.
Caveat
Asana cut the free plan to two users in November 2025 and is moving older 10-user free workspaces to the same limit, so free-tier reviews from before then are out of date.
Confidence
High

Azure Boards Work tracking inside Azure DevOps: backlogs, Kanban boards, sprints, queries and delivery plans, tied to repos and pipelines.
SoftwareMicrosoft 2018 Very large $6Free plan 1,500-2,000 4.0Mean of the six criteria: 4.0 out of 5

Azure Boards - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTasks carry Original Estimate, Remaining Work and Completed Work fields feeding capacity and burndown, but there is no timer or timesheet; those need Marketplace extensions.Time tracking: Partial. Tasks carry Original Estimate, Remaining Work and Completed Work fields feeding capacity and burndown, but there is no timer or timesheet; those need Marketplace extensions.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Not native.
SyncTwo-way calendar sync: Not native.

Summary

Azure Boards is the work-tracking part of Microsoft’s Azure DevOps, the successor to Team Foundation Server. It suits software teams already on Azure, GitHub or Visual Studio who want backlogs and sprints beside their code and pipelines.

Work items follow Agile, Scrum, CMMI or custom processes and appear in backlogs, Kanban boards, sprint taskboards and saved queries; Delivery Plans show up to 20 team backlogs on a timeline with dependencies, and dashboards and Power BI handle reporting. There is no calendar view, and time is tracked as remaining and completed hours rather than with timesheets.

Basic access is free for 5 users and then $6 a seat a month, billed through Azure. Unlimited Stakeholders are free and can edit work items and move cards on a board, but cannot reorder backlogs, plan sprints or configure boards, so whoever plans the work needs a paid seat. Visual Studio and GitHub Enterprise licences include Basic.

Organisations choose one of eight geographies, from the EU to India, and Azure DevOps Server still ships for on-premise use, with Patch 9 released in October 2026. Microsoft lists ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA and C5. AI arrives through GitHub Copilot, which can turn a work item into a draft pull request. Leaving is done by query exports or the API.

Assessment

Value for money4.3
Five free Basic users, unlimited free Stakeholders and $6 a seat after that, with repos and pipelines in the same licence.
Ease of use2.8
Process templates, area and iteration paths and query-driven views need a configured project before a team is comfortable.
Enterprise features4.6
Entra ID sign-in and conditional access, granular permissions, audit streaming, multi-organisation billing and ISO, SOC, C5 and IRAP coverage.
Interface flexibility4.2
Backlogs, boards, taskboards, delivery plans, queries, dashboards, Power BI views and custom processes; no calendar or list-style planner.
Data control4.8
Eight data geographies chosen per organisation, and Azure DevOps Server remains on sale for fully self-managed hosting.
Portability3.5
Query results export to CSV and Excel and the REST API is complete, but no one-click export of a whole organisation exists.

Record

First launched
2018. Launched as Azure Boards on 10 September 2018 within Azure DevOps, succeeding Visual Studio Team Services and the work tracking of Team Foundation Server.
Vendor
Microsoft. Publicly listed (NASDAQ: MSFT); headquartered in Redmond, Washington, USA. Azure Boards is part of the Azure DevOps Services suite.
Website
azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/devops/boards
Plans
Stakeholder free; Basic free for 5 users, then $6 per user per month; Basic + Test Plans $52 per user per month. Visual Studio subscribers and GitHub Enterprise users get Basic at no extra charge.
Free plan
The first 5 Basic users are free with Boards, Repos, one Pipelines job and 2 GiB of Artifacts; unlimited free Stakeholders can view boards and backlogs, add and edit work items and move cards, but cannot reorder backlogs, bulk edit, plan sprints or configure boards.
Hosting
Azure datacentres in a geography chosen per organisation: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Asia Pacific, EU, India, UK or US, movable later; profile data follows user location and tokens stay in the US. Azure DevOps Server is the self-managed on-premise edition, patched through October 2026.
Security
ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27018:2019, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA with BAA, EU Model Clauses, Germany C5, Australia IRAP and ENS Spain. Sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID with its SSO and conditional access; audit log (in public preview) requires Entra-backed organisations and keeps events 90 days, with streaming to Splunk or Azure.
Calendar sync
None. Work items do not publish to Google or Outlook calendars, and there is no iCal feed; Microsoft’s Team Calendar extension tracks sprints and days off rather than work items.
Data out
Query results export to CSV and import back for bulk edits; Excel integration publishes flat lists and hierarchies; Analytics views feed Power BI. Full REST APIs and service hooks. The Data Migration Tool moves Server collections into Services; whole-organisation moves elsewhere need Marketplace tools or the API.
Platforms
Web, with Visual Studio and Excel clients; no official mobile app for Boards was found. Azure DevOps Server runs on Windows Server for self-hosting.
AI
GitHub Copilot integration starts Copilot’s coding agent from a work item to create a branch and draft pull request; it requires a GitHub Copilot subscription and GitHub repositories. The Azure DevOps MCP Server, hosted in Europe and the US, passes data through without storing it.
Integrations
The Visual Studio Marketplace lists 1,698 extensions in the Azure Boards category, plus first-party links to GitHub, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Power BI and Excel; full REST APIs, service hooks and an Azure DevOps MCP Server.
Market signal
A service line of Microsoft, a public company; the Visual Studio Marketplace lists 5,436 Azure DevOps extensions, 1,698 of them for Azure Boards (November 2026); Microsoft publishes no separate Azure DevOps user count.
Caveat
The audit log is still in public preview and only works for Entra ID-backed organisations, and free Stakeholder seats can edit work items and move cards but cannot reorder backlogs or plan sprints.
Confidence
High

Google Tasks Free, minimal to-do list built into Gmail, Google Calendar and the Workspace side panel, with lists, subtasks, due dates and repeats.
PersonalGoogle 2008 Very large FreeNo paid tier 5-15 3.3Mean of the six criteria: 3.3 out of 5

Google Tasks - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Not native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Not native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Not native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncTwo-way calendar sync: Native.

Summary

Google Tasks is a bare to-do list that lives inside Gmail, Google Calendar and the Workspace side panel, with mobile apps for Android and iOS. It suits people who already plan their day in Google Calendar and want tasks beside their events, not a separate system.

A task has a title, details, a start date and time with a duration, a deadline, a repeat rule, a star and subtasks, and sits in a list. Dated tasks show on the Calendar grid, an email can become a task, and Workspace users can assign group tasks in Chat spaces and Docs. There are no labels, priorities, shared lists, board or timeline.

There is nothing to buy: a personal Google account gets the whole product. Organisations get it with any Workspace edition, from Business Starter at $7 a user per month on an annual plan, which adds administrator control rather than task features.

For Workspace customers Tasks data is covered by Google’s ISO 27001 and SOC 2 scope and by data region policies on Business Standard and above; Gemini can create tasks from any Workspace side panel since September 2026, and Google says prompts are not used for training without permission. Leaving is simple but thin: Takeout gives JSON for the whole account, there is no CSV, and nothing imports in.

Assessment

Value for money5.0
Free with any Google account and already included in every Workspace plan, with no caps a person is likely to meet.
Ease of use4.8
The simplest tool here: a list, a date and a star, reachable from the Gmail and Calendar side panel.
Enterprise features2.5
Workspace admins can switch Tasks on or off and apply SSO and data regions, but Tasks itself has no roles or reporting.
Interface flexibility1.3
Lists, subtasks, stars, deadlines and a calendar display; no labels, priorities, board, custom fields or automation.
Data control3.8
Workspace lists Tasks under ISO 27001 and SOC 2 and data regions from Business Standard; personal accounts get no region choice.
Portability2.5
Google Takeout gives a JSON export of every list and the REST API is free, but there is no CSV or importer.

Record

First launched
2008. Launched as a Gmail Labs feature in December 2008; the standalone mobile app followed in April 2018.
Vendor
Google LLC, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL). Publicly traded, headquartered in Mountain View, California, USA.
Website
tasks.google.com
Plans
Free with a personal Google account; included in every Google Workspace edition (Business Starter $7, Standard $14, Plus $22 per user per month on annual plans), where the administrator controls access.
Free plan
Every Tasks feature is free with a Google account, up to 100,000 tasks in total and 20,000 open tasks per list; group tasks in Chat spaces and assigning from Docs need an eligible Workspace account.
Hosting
Google’s own data centres. Workspace Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise, Frontline and Education Standard/Plus editions can apply a data region policy to Tasks data at rest; personal accounts have no choice. No self-managed edition.
Security
Google lists Workspace services including Tasks in scope for ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and SOC 1, 2 and 3. SSO, MFA and audit sit at the Google Workspace account level; administrators control access to Tasks, but Tasks has no roles of its own.
Calendar sync
Native: tasks with dates appear in Google Calendar on web and mobile, and edits in either place apply to the same task. Repeating tasks show a limited number of upcoming instances. No Outlook sync and no iCal feed.
Data out
Google Takeout exports the whole account’s Tasks as JSON (third-party guides disagree on whether it is one file or one per list), with titles, notes, due dates, completion, order and subtask links; no CSV and no scheduled backups. The Google Tasks REST API reads and writes lists and tasks. No importers.
Platforms
Web (inside Google Calendar and the side panel of Gmail, Chat, Drive, Docs, Sheets and Slides), Android, iOS and ChromeOS. No desktop app for Windows, macOS or Linux.
AI
Gemini in the Workspace side panels can create reminders and to-do lists in Google Tasks since September 2026, on Business and Enterprise Standard and Plus and on Google AI Pro and Ultra. Google states Workspace prompts are customer data and not used for training without permission.
Integrations
Gmail (email to task), Google Calendar, Chat spaces, Docs, Drive, Keep reminders and Gemini; third parties connect through the public Google Tasks REST API, which has no webhooks.
Market signal
Google publishes no Tasks user count; the service ships inside Gmail, Google Calendar, Chat, Drive and Docs for every Google account and Workspace customer, a product line of Alphabet (checked November 2026).
Caveat
Google Tasks has had no official feature announcements in 2026 beyond a widget redesign; a search bar and a “Plan your day” view have only appeared in app teardowns.
Confidence
Medium-high

Jira Issue and project tracker built around configurable workflows, with backlog, board, timeline, list and calendar views and a 6,000-app marketplace.
SoftwareAtlassian 2002 Very large $7.92†Free plan 6,000+ 4.0Mean of the six criteria: 4.0 out of 5

Jira - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncTwo-way calendar sync: Not native.

Summary

Jira tracks work as issues, now called work items, moving through workflows that an administrator defines, and it remains the default tracker in large software organisations. Atlassian also sells it to marketing, operations and other business teams on the same plans.

Every plan has backlog, board, list, timeline, calendar and summary views, custom fields and workflows, and JQL queries that feed dashboards and reports. The timeline shows dependencies within one project; plans across projects, capacity and scenario modelling are Premium. What it lacks out of the box is calendar sync and a timesheet, both of which arrive through the Marketplace.

The free plan stops at 10 users and 2 GB. Prices rose by about 7% on 13 October 2026: Standard is $9.70 per user a month billed monthly for the first 100 users, about $7.92 billed annually, and Premium $19.60. Rovo AI is included on paid plans with monthly credit allowances (25, 70 and 150 per user); SSO and SCIM need an Atlassian Guard subscription below Enterprise.

Data can be pinned to 11 residency locations from Standard upwards. Since 17 August 2026 Atlassian uses de-identified, aggregated metadata from Free, Standard and Premium sites to improve its apps and AI features, and only Enterprise can switch that off; in-app content is also contributed by default on Free and Standard unless an admin turns it off. Leaving is realistic: CSV, XML and Word exports, a full backup with attachments and complete APIs.

Assessment

Value for money3.5
Ten free users and Standard at about $7.92 a user billed annually, but advanced planning needs Premium and SSO needs Atlassian Guard.
Ease of use2.8
Schemes, workflows, screens and JQL reward an administrator; newcomers face unfamiliar terms before the first sprint.
Enterprise features4.8

2002. First release of Jira as downloadable software in 2002, the year Atlassian was founded; Jira Cloud followed later.

Atlassian. Publicly listed (NASDAQ: TEAM); founded in Sydney, Australia, in 2002, incorporated in Delaware since 2022, with headquarters in Sydney and San Francisco.

atlassian.com/software/jira

Free for up to 10 users; Standard $9.70 per user a month billed monthly, or $950 a year for 10 users (about $7.92 per user a month); Premium $19.60 per user billed monthly, or $1,950 a year for 10 users; Enterprise annual only, with published list prices from $179,000 a year for 1,000 users. Monthly per-user rates fall in higher user bands.
Free plan
Up to 10 users with 2 GB storage, every core view, 150 automation steps a month and community support; no Rovo AI, permissions or audit log.

Atlassian Cloud on AWS. Data residency on Standard, Premium and Enterprise in Australia, Canada, EU, Germany, India, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Switzerland, UK and USA. REST APIs and webhooks on all plans; direct importers for Asana and Trello, plus CSV and JSON import.

Web, iOS and Android. The official Jira Cloud for Mac app is no longer supported.
AI
Rovo Search, Chat and Agents on Standard, Premium and Enterprise, metered by monthly credits (25, 70 and 150 per user); not on Free. Atlassian says its LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and self-hosted open models) do not store or train on inputs. Separately, from 17 August 2026 Atlassian uses contributed data, de-identified and aggregated, to improve its apps and AI experiences: metadata is always contributed on Free, Standard and Premium and can be turned off only on Enterprise; in-app data is on by default on Free and Standard (admins can turn it off) and off by default on Premium and Enterprise.
Integrations
The Atlassian Marketplace lists more than 6,000 Cloud apps (October 2026), including Tempo, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Microsoft Teams and Figma; public REST APIs, webhooks, the Forge app platform and a Rovo MCP server on paid plans.
Market signal
Atlassian reported FY2026 revenue of $6,572 million and 350,000+ customers (Q4 FY2026 results, 6 August 2026), with Jira as its flagship product line.

Jira Data Center stopped selling to new customers on 30 March 2026 and goes read-only on 28 March 2029, so Cloud is now the only edition a new buyer can choose.

Microsoft Planner Microsoft 365’s task and project planner: boards and schedules in every suite, with Gantt timelines, sprints and goals from Planner Plan 1.
TeamsMicrosoft 2016 Very large $10No free plan 10-30 3.9Mean of the six criteria: 3.9 out of 5

Microsoft Planner - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Not native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncA plan’s schedule can be published as an iCalendar feed into Outlook; it is one-way and there is no Google Calendar sync.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. A plan’s schedule can be published as an iCalendar feed into Outlook; it is one-way and there is no Google Calendar sync.

Summary

Microsoft Planner is the task and project tool inside Microsoft 365, reached from the web, Teams and Outlook. Since August 2025 it also carries what used to be Project for the web, so one app now spans a team’s shared board and a scheduled project.

Basic plans give tasks with buckets, checklists, labels and attachments in grid, board, schedule and charts views, plus My Day and My Tasks. Premium plans add a timeline (Gantt) view with dependencies, sprints and backlogs, goals, custom fields and a people view; Plan 3 adds critical path, baselines, roadmaps and an assignments view. There is no time tracking, and premium plans top out at 3,000 tasks each.

Most organisations already have basic Planner through a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 suite. Planner Plan 1 costs $10 per user per month paid annually and Planner and Project Plan 3 costs $30; Planner’s subscriptions page now lists only those two premium plans, and Project Online retired on 30 September 2026. Copilot and the Planner Agent need a separate Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.

Basic plan data sits in Azure in the tenant’s geography and premium plans in Dataverse, under Microsoft’s certifications and data protection addendum; Planner does not take part in Advanced Data Residency or support customer-managed keys. Leaving means Excel exports, an admin PowerShell JSON export or the Graph API.

Assessment

Value for money3.5
Boards come free with most Microsoft 365 suites, but timelines cost $10 a seat and critical path $30.
Ease of use4.3
Basic plans are a card board inside Teams and Outlook that most Microsoft 365 users can pick up unaided.
Enterprise features4.2
Entra ID sign-in, Purview audit logs and eDiscovery, but no Planner admin roles and eDiscovery only for basic group plans.
Interface flexibility4.0
Grid, board, schedule, charts, timeline, people and goals views, sprints and custom fields, with Power Automate behind premium plans.
Data control4.0
Data follows the tenant’s geography (Europe, Americas, Asia-Pacific, Australia, Canada, Japan or India), with no residency commitment or customer-managed keys.
Portability3.5
Export to Excel per plan, admin JSON export per user and the Graph API; .mpp import was removed in 2025.

Record

First launched
2016. General availability in Office 365 on 6 June 2016; Project for the web was folded into it on 1 August 2025.
Vendor
Microsoft Corporation. Public company (NASDAQ: MSFT), headquartered in Redmond, Washington, US.
Website
microsoft.com/microsoft-365/planner
Plans
Basic Planner inside Microsoft 365 and Office 365 suites; Planner Plan 1 at $10 and Planner and Project Plan 3 at $30 per user per month paid annually. Planner and Project Plan 5 (formerly $55) is still named in Microsoft’s Project for the web service description but no longer on Planner’s subscriptions page, which lists only Plan 1 and Plan 3.
Free plan
No standalone free plan; basic Planner (grid, board, schedule and charts views) is included in Microsoft 365 Business Basic and higher suites, but timeline, goals and sprints need Plan 1.
Hosting
Microsoft Azure. Basic plans are stored by the tenant’s default geography: Europe, Americas or Asia-Pacific macro-regions, with local storage for Australia, Canada, India and Japan (UK tenants map to Europe); Microsoft makes no specific residency commitment for Planner and it does not take part in Advanced Data Residency. Premium plans are stored in Dataverse. No on-premise edition (Project Server is a separate product).
Security
Covered by Microsoft 365’s audit reports on the Service Trust Portal, the Product Terms and the Data Protection Addendum. Sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID with its SSO and provisioning; Purview audit logs on all plans, eDiscovery only for basic group plans, no retention policies, and Purview needs an E5-class licence.
Calendar sync
One-way iCalendar publishing of a plan’s schedule to the Outlook calendar (any iCal client can subscribe); assigned tasks also show in Microsoft To Do. No Google Calendar sync and nothing flows back.
Data out
Export a plan to Excel from the web app; global admins can export a user’s plans as JSON with the Export-PlannerUserContent PowerShell cmdlet. Planner API in Microsoft Graph for basic plans; premium plan data is reachable through Dataverse. Direct .mpp import was removed when Project for the web retired.
Platforms
Web, Planner in Teams (Windows, macOS, Linux via the Teams client), Outlook integration, iOS and Android apps.
AI
Copilot in Planner and the Planner Agent (Project Manager agent) require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, with more capability for Plan 1 or Plan 3 holders. Microsoft states prompts, responses and Microsoft Graph data are not used to train foundation models, and EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary.
Integrations
Built into Teams, Outlook, To Do, SharePoint and Loop, with Power Automate flows and Power BI reporting on premium plans; the Planner API in Microsoft Graph covers basic plans, premium plans live in Dataverse, and a Planner MCP server is documented.
Market signal
Bundled with Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Standard and Premium, Office 365 E1, E3 and E5 and Microsoft 365 A1 (Microsoft Learn, October 2026); Microsoft publishes no Planner-only user count.
Caveat
Microsoft’s own price pages blocked automated access for this review; the $10 and $30 figures are Microsoft’s list prices as quoted in October 2026, and no formal end-of-sale notice for Plan 5 was found.
Confidence
Medium-high

Microsoft To Do Free personal task list from Microsoft with My Day, smart lists and steps, stored in Exchange Online and woven into Outlook and Teams.
PersonalMicrosoft 2017 Very large FreeNo paid tier 5-15 3.3Mean of the six criteria: 3.3 out of 5

Microsoft To Do - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Not native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Not native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Not native.
CalCalendar view: Not native.
SyncIn new Outlook and Outlook on the web a task can be dragged from the My Day pane onto the Outlook calendar to book time; it is a one-way copy and Google Calendar is not supported.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. In new Outlook and Outlook on the web a task can be dragged from the My Day pane onto the Outlook calendar to book time; it is a one-way copy and Google Calendar is not supported.

Summary

Microsoft To Do is a plain personal task list built by the former Wunderlist team and given away with every Microsoft account. It suits people who live in Outlook and want their own tasks, flagged email and assigned Planner tasks in one place.

Tasks sit in lists and groups, with steps, notes, due dates, reminders, recurrence and file attachments; My Day is a daily shortlist that empties each night. There is no board, calendar view, timeline, custom field or automation inside the app. Lists can be shared, but there is no assignment workflow worth the name.

There is nothing to buy. Personal accounts get everything free, and organisations get To Do with any Microsoft 365 plan that includes an Exchange Online mailbox; on-premise Exchange is not supported.

Tasks are stored in the user’s Exchange Online mailbox, so work accounts inherit Microsoft 365 encryption, certifications and tenant data location, and admins can find tasks with Purview eDiscovery. Copilot Premium users can read and edit To Do tasks through the Planner Agent since July 2026. Leaving is awkward: there is no export button, only a whole-mailbox PST from Outlook or the Graph API. Microsoft’s task investment has shifted to Planner, and from December 2026 private tasks created in Planner stop landing in To Do.

Assessment

Value for money5.0
Entirely free with a personal Microsoft account and already paid for in most Microsoft 365 work plans.
Ease of use4.7
My Day, smart lists and steps are learnt in minutes, and flagged Outlook email turns up as tasks without setup.
Enterprise features2.5
Work accounts inherit Entra ID sign-in, licence control and Purview eDiscovery, but To Do itself has no team admin or roles.
Interface flexibility1.5
Lists, My Day and smart lists only: no board, calendar view, custom fields or automation inside the app.
Data control3.8
Tasks live in the Exchange Online mailbox under Microsoft 365 certifications and tenant data location; personal accounts get no region choice.
Portability2.0
No export button; data leaves through an Outlook PST export, admin eDiscovery or the Graph API, and there are no importers.

Record

First launched
2017. Public preview released in April 2017 by the former Wunderlist team as Wunderlist’s successor.
Vendor
Microsoft Corporation. Publicly traded (NASDAQ: MSFT), headquartered in Redmond, Washington, USA; To Do came from the team behind Wunderlist, acquired in 2015.
Website
microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/microsoft-to-do-list-app
Plans
Free with a personal Microsoft account; included in Microsoft 365 Family and Personal, and in Business Essentials, Business Premium, E1 to E5, F2 and Education A1 to A5 plans that carry Exchange Online.
Free plan
Every feature is free with a personal Microsoft account, with no list or task caps published; work and school use needs a qualifying Microsoft 365 licence with Exchange Online.
Hosting
Stored and synced in Exchange Online, so work and school data follows the Microsoft 365 tenant’s data location; personal accounts use Microsoft’s consumer cloud with no choice. No on-premise edition: on-premise Exchange mailboxes have been unsupported since March 2021.
Security
Encrypted at rest on Exchange servers and in transit. Work accounts inherit Microsoft 365 compliance commitments (ISO 27001, ISO 27018, GDPR, EU Data Boundary), Entra ID sign-in with SSO and MFA, per-user licence control and Purview eDiscovery; To Do has no admin console of its own.
Calendar sync
No calendar view or feed. In new Outlook and Outlook on the web, tasks can be dragged from the My Day pane onto the Outlook calendar as a time block (one-way). No Google Calendar sync.
Data out
No in-app export. Personal users export the whole mailbox to PST from desktop Outlook; admins export tasks as PST via Purview content search. The Microsoft Graph To Do API reads and writes lists, tasks and checklist items. No importers.
Platforms
Web, iOS, Android, Windows and macOS, plus Outlook (web, new Outlook, mobile) and Teams. No Linux app.
AI
No AI inside the To Do app. Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium users can query and edit To Do tasks through the Planner Agent since July 2026; Microsoft states prompts, responses and Graph data are not used to train foundation models.
Integrations
Outlook tasks and flagged email, Planner assigned tasks, Teams, Microsoft Launcher, Power Automate and Zapier; the Microsoft Graph To Do API covers lists, tasks, checklist items and linked resources for personal and work accounts.
Market signal
Microsoft publishes no To Do user count; its Graph documentation (updated August 2025) says To Do reaches “millions of users”, and the app ships inside Outlook and Teams for Microsoft 365 work accounts as part of a major public company’s product line.
Caveat
Microsoft is moving task management towards Planner: Windows Latest called To Do effectively in maintenance mode in August 2026, and from December 2026 private tasks created in Planner no longer appear in To Do, though no retirement has been announced.

Medium-high

monday work management - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.

Summary

monday work management is the core product of monday.com, alongside the separate CRM, dev and service products built on the same platform. It is sold to teams of any type that want to model their own process rather than adopt a fixed project method.

Everything lives on boards: rows are items, columns are typed fields such as status, people, date or formula, and the same board can be shown as a table, Kanban, timeline, Gantt chart, calendar or chart. Automations, dashboards and Workdocs connect boards together. There is no native Scrum layer in this product; sprints are sold separately in monday dev.

The free plan is for 2 seats and 3 boards, so it is a trial in practice. Every paid plan starts at 3 seats and is sold in seat buckets. Basic at $9 a seat lacks timeline, calendar, automations and integrations, so most teams need Standard at $12; time tracking, private boards, dependencies and workload sit on Pro at $19. AI runs on monthly credits (1,000 on Basic, 2,000 on Standard, 3,000 on Pro), with more available to buy.

Data is hosted on AWS in the US, Germany or Australia, with the region set by where the account is opened, and monday.com holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certificates. SSO, SCIM, audit logs and strict EU residency are Enterprise features, and the Guardian add-on adds tenant keys and BYOK. monday.com states customer data is not used to train AI models. Boards export to Excel and the GraphQL API is complete, but Workdocs and dashboards are left out of the account export.

Assessment

Value for money2.5
A 3-seat minimum and seat buckets; timeline needs Standard at $12 and time tracking needs Pro at $19.
Ease of use4.3
Colour-coded boards and templates get a team working on day one; cross-board structures take planning.
Enterprise features4.6
SAML SSO, SCIM, audit log, multi-level permissions, portfolios and resource management, all on Enterprise only.
Interface flexibility4.6
More than 30 column types, many board views, dashboards across up to 50 boards, automations and an apps framework.
Data control4.5
US, EU (Germany) or Australian hosting, strict EU residency and BYOK through the Guardian add-on on Enterprise.
Portability3.6
Boards export to Excel with updates; admins get a zip of all boards and files; a full GraphQL API.

2014. Commercial launch as daPulse in 2014; renamed monday.com in November 2017.

monday.com Ltd. Publicly listed on Nasdaq (MNDY); headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel.

Free plan
Free for up to 2 seats, 3 boards and 3 docs with 8 column types; no timeline, calendar, automations, integrations or guests.
Hosting
AWS in three regions: United States, European Union (Germany) and Asia Pacific (Australia). Notion Workspace of pages and databases: wikis, docs and task databases shown as table, board, timeline or calendar, with AI agents built in.
TeamsNotion Labs 2016 Very large $10Free plan 80-150 4.2Mean of the six criteria: 4.2 out of 5

Notion - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Not native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncNotion Calendar shows and edits database dates beside Google or iCloud events, but tasks are never written into Google or Outlook calendars and there is no iCal feed.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. Notion Calendar shows and edits database dates beside Google or iCloud events, but tasks are never written into Google or Outlook calendars and there is no iCal feed.

Summary

Notion combines documents, wikis and databases in one editor, so a project plan, its meeting notes and the task list behind it can live on the same page. It is used both by individuals and by whole companies as their internal knowledge base and planning tool.

Everything is a page made of blocks, and databases are pages whose rows are pages. A task database can be shown as a table, board, timeline with dependencies, calendar, list, gallery or chart, and linked to other databases through relations. Notion supplies templates rather than a fixed task model, so assignment, status and recurrence are whatever a team builds. There is no time tracking.

Free suits a single person; teams of two or more hit the block limit. Plus at $10 removes it. Since 13 May 2025 full Notion AI (the Notion Agent, meeting notes and enterprise search) comes only with Business at $20 and Enterprise, and Custom Agents are billed separately at $10 per 1,000 credits. Business also adds SAML SSO and private teamspaces.

Notion holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001, 27018 and 27701, and offers data residency in the US, EU, Japan or Korea on Enterprise; customer-managed keys (Enterprise Key Management) are still a beta for selected Enterprise customers. It states customer data is not used to train AI models; LLM providers keep data 30 days except on Enterprise, where retention is zero. Workspace export to Markdown, CSV and HTML with uploaded files makes leaving realistic, though relations and views do not survive.

Assessment

Value for money3.6
Free is generous for one person and Plus is $10, but full AI, SSO and Agents need Business at $20.
Ease of use3.8
Writing a page is instant; building a working task system from blank databases takes deliberate design.
Enterprise features4.6
SAML SSO on Business; SCIM, audit log, DLP and SIEM connections, residency and beta key management on Enterprise.
Interface flexibility4.6
Table, board, timeline, calendar, list, gallery, chart and form views, relations, database automations and an API.
Data control4.4
Residency in the US, EU, Japan or Korea on Enterprise; customer-managed keys exist only as a beta for selected Enterprise customers.
Portability4.3
Any plan exports the whole workspace to Markdown, CSV or HTML with files; importers cover Asana, Trello and Confluence.

Record

First launched

Summary

Smartsheet looks like a spreadsheet but behaves like a project tool: each row is a task with owners, dates, dependencies and attachments. It is bought mostly by large organisations and their PMOs, and by operations teams that already think in rows and columns.

A sheet can be shown as a grid, Gantt chart, board, calendar or table, and reports and dashboards roll many sheets together. Formulas, cross-sheet references, forms, approval workflows and no-code WorkApps let teams build their own systems. Much of the advanced range is sold separately: Resource Management (which holds time tracking), Dynamic View from $125 a month, Data Shuttle from $100 a month, DataMesh, Calendar App and Brandfolder.

There is no free plan. Pro at $9 suits a small team of up to 10 Members but lacks the API, timeline view and scheduled backups. Business at $19 needs 3 Members and adds those, plus unlimited automations and workload tracking. SAML SSO, portfolios and directory integration require Enterprise.

Data can sit in the US, the EU (Germany) or Australia through Smartsheet Regions, and a separate Smartsheet Gov runs on AWS GovCloud. Smartsheet lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, 27701 and 42001, with a FedRAMP Moderate authorisation for Smartsheet Gov, and says third parties never train foundation models on customer data. Backups on Business and above are Excel workbooks with comments and uploaded attachments, but formulas, reports and dashboards do not travel.

The grid feels like a spreadsheet, but formulas, cross-sheet references and workflows reward trained builders.
Enterprise features4.9

Interface flexibility4.4
Grid, Gantt, board, calendar, table and timeline views, dashboards, reports, forms, automations and no-code WorkApps.
Data control4.6
US, EU (Germany) or Australian regions, a GovCloud edition and customer-managed encryption keys as an add-on.
Portability3.4

Trello - summary, assessment and sources

Summary

Trello is the board most people meet first: lists running left to right, cards moving between them. Atlassian sells it to any team that wants shared visual task lists without the weight of a project tool such as Jira.

Cards carry checklists, due dates, labels, attachments and custom fields, and Butler automation moves them by rule. Power-Ups add almost everything else, from Gantt charts to time tracking, which Trello does not build in. Calendar, Timeline, Table, Dashboard and Map views belong to Premium, and the Timeline has no dependencies. Planner pulls Google or Outlook events beside your cards and schedules focus time back into the calendar.

The free plan is generous on cards and Power-Ups but, since May 2024, a free Workspace with more than 10 collaborators (members, guests and pending invites) turns view-only. Standard at $5 removes the board and collaborator caps; most teams wanting more than boards will need Premium at $10.

Content is held in Atlassian’s US AWS regions, with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 coverage. AI features (board generation, checklists, smart scheduling) are on by default on paid plans. Export is JSON per board for everyone, CSV and Workspace exports with attachments for Premium, and the public API is open on all plans.

Assessment

A free plan for 10 collaborators and $5 Standard, but calendar, timeline and table views need $10 Premium.
Ease of use4.8
Lists and cards on a board are learnt in minutes; the model has barely changed since 2011.
Enterprise features3.5
Enterprise adds SSO and provisioning through Atlassian Guard and SOC 2 reports, but little portfolio reporting.
Interface flexibility3.5
Five extra views, custom fields and Butler automation exist, though most depth arrives through 200 Power-Ups.
Data control3.0
SOC 2 and ISO 27001 under Atlassian, but content sits in US AWS regions with no residency choice.
Portability3.5
JSON board export on every plan is capped at 1,000 actions; CSV and full Workspace export need Premium.

One-way each direction: an iCal feed out of a calendar view, and Google or Outlook Calendar sync into a table; events can be updated back only by building automations.

Summary

Airtable is a no-code database: each base holds linked tables of typed fields, and teams build their own trackers, content calendars and lightweight apps on top. It suits operations, marketing and product teams who outgrow spreadsheets but do not want a fixed project tool.

Any table can be viewed as a grid, Kanban board, calendar, gallery, form, timeline or Gantt chart, and Interfaces turn bases into custom screens for people who should not see the raw data. Automations, scripting and the Omni AI assistant sit across the whole base. It is not a task manager out of the box: assignment, recurrence and time tracking have to be modelled.

Free allows 5 editors and 1,000 records a base, which suits a trial or a small project. Team at $20 a seat raises that to 50,000 records with Gantt and timeline views; Business at $45 adds SSO, the admin panel and two-way sync between bases. AI runs on monthly credits (15,000 per seat on Team), with top-ups from $20 per 10,000.

Airtable holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 and 27701 certificates. Data residency in the US, Europe or Australia and customer-managed keys are Enterprise Scale features, and its AI terms bar Airtable and its model providers from training on customer data. Export is CSV per view, so a full exit means using the API. Bending Spoons completed its purchase of Airtable on 4 September 2026 and let go a large part of the pre-acquisition team in October; it says nothing changes for customers’ plans or prices.

A free plan for 5 editors and 1,000 records a base, then $20 a seat, and $45 for SSO and admin.

The grid is familiar at once, but linked tables, interfaces and automations ask for database thinking.
Enterprise features4.5
SAML SSO and admin panel on Business; audit logs, EKM, residency and org units on Enterprise Scale.

Grid, Kanban, calendar, gallery, form, list, timeline and Gantt views, interfaces, automations, scripting and extensions.
Data control4.5
US, EU or Australian residency and customer-owned AWS KMS keys, both on Enterprise Scale only.
Portability3.2
CSV per view only, without comments; the full REST API and webhooks are the real exit.

Google, Outlook and iCloud events are mirrored into Any.do on all plans; tasks reach Google Calendar only when scheduled as time blocks, and no edit-back from the external calendar to the task is documented. Summary

Any.do is a to-do list and daily planner that puts tasks next to the events of your existing calendar, with reminders that can arrive on WhatsApp. It is aimed at individuals and households first, with a Teams plan for small groups who want shared boards.

Personal plans offer lists, subtasks, My Day and a calendar view that mirrors Google, Outlook or iCloud events. Family adds shared boards and a grocery list. Teams adds Kanban, table, calendar and Gantt views, custom fields, task chat, rule automations and time tracking, though the help centre documents few details of the last two.

The free plan has no task cap but holds back recurring tasks, WhatsApp reminders, tags and AI. Premium is $4.99 a month billed annually, and Teams is the same per member with no stated minimum, which makes it one of the cheaper shared boards. Importers from Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Monday and Todoist need Family or Teams.

Data protection is thinly documented: the vendor names no hosting provider, region or certification, and states encryption in transit only. An MCP server lets ChatGPT and Claude read and edit tasks on every plan. Leaving is easier from boards, which export to CSV or Excel, than from personal lists, which print to PDF or export archived tasks as CSV.

Boards export to CSV or Excel on Family and Teams, but personal lists print only to PDF; no REST API.

First launched
2011. First public app release; the vendor’s homepage says it has been helping people for 15 years as of 2026.
Vendor
Any.do Inc. and affiliates. Privately held; the privacy policy relies on Israel’s EU adequacy decision for data transfers, pointing to operations in Israel, but publishes no head office address.

any.do

Basecamp - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTimesheets with CSV reports exist only on Pro Plus and Pro Unlimited, and hours are logged manually without a running timer.Time tracking: Partial. Timesheets with CSV reports exist only on Pro Plus and Pro Unlimited, and hours are logged manually without a running timer.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttLineup shows whole projects as bars on a rolling 13-week timeline; there are no task-level bars or dependencies.Gantt or dependency timeline: Partial. Lineup shows whole projects as bars on a rolling 13-week timeline; there are no task-level bars or dependencies.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncOne-way iCal subscription to Google, Apple, Outlook or HEY calendars; changes made outside Basecamp do not flow back.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. One-way iCal subscription to Google, Apple, Outlook or HEY calendars; changes made outside Basecamp do not flow back.

Summary

Basecamp organises work as projects, each a page of tools: a message board, to-do lists, a Kanban card table, group chat, docs and files, and scheduled check-ins. It is built for small companies, agencies and anyone who invites clients into the work.

Basecamp 5, released in 2026, added subtasks, a global calendar, account-wide Everything pages and Markdown in documents. Planning stays deliberately light: hill charts show progress by feel, and Lineup places whole projects on a 13-week timeline. There are no custom fields, automations, dependencies or dashboards, and time tracking is a manual timesheet.

Pricing is a flat monthly fee for the account rather than per seat. Freelancer at $29 covers five users and three active projects; Pro at $79 and Pro Plus at $99 raise those to 10 and 15 users. Pro Unlimited, $199 a month billed annually, removes the caps and is the only package with annual billing and the Admin Pro Pack. Large teams pay little per head; a seven-person team with ten live projects already needs Pro Plus.

Data sits on 37signals’ own servers in the United States after its 2023 exit from the public cloud, with no residency choice and no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate. There are no built-in AI features, and the privacy policy says content is not used to train models. Leaving means an HTML archive of every project plus files, or the public API.

Assessment

Value for money3.8
Flat pricing from $29 a month for five users gets cheap per head, but project caps and a one-project free plan bite.
Ease of use4.6
Every project is the same toolbox of messages, to-dos, cards and chat, so new people and clients orient in minutes.
Enterprise features1.8
The vendor states it supports no SSO or SAML, no SCIM, and only the top package adds permission restrictions and enforced 2FA.
Interface flexibility2.5
Lists, card tables, a calendar and hill charts, but no custom fields, automations or dashboards.
Data control2.0
Runs on 37signals’ own hardware in the United States, with no SOC 2 or ISO 27001, only self-assessed questionnaires.
Portability3.0
An owner-only HTML export with files covers every project and the API is complete, but tasks never export as CSV or JSON.

First launched
2004. Public launch of Basecamp by 37signals in 2004; the current version, Basecamp 5, shipped in 2026.
Vendor
37signals LLC. Privately held and self-funded, based in Chicago, United States; also makes HEY and Fizzy.
Website
basecamp.com
Plans
Basecamp Personal, free (1 project, 3 users); Freelancer $29/month (3 active projects, 5 users, 10 GB); Pro $79/month (8 projects, 10 users, 25 GB); Pro Plus $99/month (12 projects, 15 users, 100 GB, time tracking); Pro Unlimited $199/month billed annually or $329 monthly (unlimited projects and users, 1 TB, Admin Pro Pack).
Free plan
Basecamp Personal is free for one project, three users and 1 GB of storage, without templates, time tracking or multiple tools per project.
Hosting
37signals’ own servers in colocation facilities, primarily in the United States; no EU or other region choice and no self-managed edition.
Security
No SOC 2 or ISO 27001; PCI DSS SAQ A self-assessment, published CSA CAIQ v4.1 and HECVAT 4 questionnaires, DPA on request. No SSO, SAML or SCIM; Google sign-in and 2FA available, with enforced 2FA and permission restrictions in the Admin Pro Pack on Pro Unlimited.
Calendar sync
One-way iCal subscription of the global or a project calendar (events, or events plus assignments) into Google, Apple, Outlook or HEY; updates can take a few hours. All plans.
Data out
Account owners can export the whole account, selected projects or Ping conversations as an HTML archive including files and comments; timesheets export as CSV; full REST API with webhooks, SDKs and a CLI. The HTML export cannot be re-imported.
Platforms
Web; iOS and Android apps; desktop apps for macOS and Windows; installable PWA in Chrome (including Linux), Safari and Edge.
AI
No built-in AI features process customer content. Users can connect their own agents through the CLI or the ChatGPT and Claude MCP connectors on all plans; 37signals says content is not used to train AI models.
Integrations
The integrations directory lists roughly 100 third-party tools, mostly time trackers (Harvest, Clockify, Everhour), Zapier, Zoho Flow and Unito; there is a public REST API with webhooks, official SDKs, a CLI and an MCP connector for ChatGPT and Claude.

Basecamp’s homepage (November 2026) claims 84 million accounts and 60 million projects created to date, and says nearly a million people and organisations rely on it daily.

Basecamp’s packages changed during 2026 and its help centre still names plans (Studio, Unlimited) that no longer appear on the pricing page; only Pro Unlimited can be billed annually.

High

Summary

Bitrix24 is a business suite in which tasks and projects share a workspace with CRM, chat, video calls, documents, sites and HR tools. It is sold to small and mid-sized organisations that want one vendor for most of their software.

The tasks module offers list, Kanban, planner, calendar and Gantt views with four dependency types, plus subtasks, checklists, templates, recurring tasks and automation rules. Scrum boards, full time tracking and workload reports arrive on Professional. The breadth is also the cost: the task manager is one item in a long menu, and the interface carries every other module with it.

Pricing is a flat monthly fee per organisation. The free plan has no user cap but stops at 5 GB and one admin. Standard at $99 a month (annual) covers 50 users; Professional at $199 covers 100. Since 1 September 2026 each plan has a cheaper Essentials version without REST API, MCP server or unlimited AI, and a Vibe+ version with them; monthly and quarterly customers move to Essentials limits on 30 November 2026, annual ones at their next renewal.

Cloud data sits on AWS in Virginia or Frankfurt, chosen by the account’s regional domain, and an EU DPA is offered. The self-hosted edition (from $3,590, renewed yearly at half price) includes source code. CoPilot AI is on all plans, sends requests to OpenAI in the USA, and the terms let AI providers use content for development. Leaving the cloud means Excel exports or the API on a Vibe+ plan.

Free with no user cap, then flat fees: $99 a month covers 50 users; Scrum and full time tracking need $199.
Ease of use2.5
Tasks sit inside a crowded suite of CRM, chat, sites and HR tools, and new users face a dense menu.
Enterprise features3.4
SAML SSO, login history and branch accounts only on Enterprise from $399; certifications cited are AWS’s, not Bitrix24’s own.
Interface flexibility4.6

Data control3.8

Portability3.0
Task lists export to Excel and import from CSV, but the REST API now needs a Vibe+ plan.

Summary

ClickUp tries to replace a team’s task manager, documents, chat and whiteboard with one Workspace, organised as Spaces, Folders, Lists and tasks. It is sold to teams of every size, and its free plan is a common starting point for small companies.

Few rivals match its range: tasks carry custom statuses, fields and dependencies, and any List can be shown as a list, board, calendar, Gantt chart, table, timeline, workload or mind map. Sprints, native time tracking, goals and dashboards are built in. The cost of that range is density; settings overlap and new users often need a guided setup.

Between late October and November 2026 ClickUp replaced its Unlimited plan with Core at $9 a user and lifted Business to $17 a user on yearly billing, adding a $100 Max plan. Free stays usable for small teams but stops at 60 MB of storage and 100 automation actions. Business is where timeline, workload, dashboards and timesheets live. AI is now included as pooled monthly credits per user, with top-ups at $10 per 10,000 credits.

ClickUp holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 and 42001 certificates, and offers residency in the US, Ireland, Australia or Singapore on Enterprise. It states that AI partners may neither train on nor retain customer data. Admins can export all tasks to CSV, and importers cover most rivals, though Docs cannot be bulk-exported.

Assessment

Value for money3.8
A free plan with unlimited members and no seat minimum, but timeline, workload and dashboards now need Business at $17.
Ease of use3.1
The five-level hierarchy, dozens of toggles and overlapping features take real setup before a team settles in.
Enterprise features4.6
SAML, SCIM, audit trails, custom roles and data residency on Enterprise, with ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certification.
Interface flexibility4.9
List, board, calendar, Gantt, timeline, table, workload, mind map, map and team views, plus automations and dashboards.
Data control4.0
US, EU, Australian or Singapore hosting on Enterprise at no extra cost; no customer-managed keys or self-hosting.
Portability3.8
Admins export the Workspace to CSV with comments and attachment links; importers for Asana, Jira, Trello and monday.

AWS. Data residency for core Workspace data in the United States, Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Australia) or Asia Pacific (Singapore) on Enterprise at no extra cost. No self-managed or on-premise edition.

Docs export one at a time to PDF, HTML or Markdown; bulk Docs export is not available. Public REST API (100 requests a minute per token below Enterprise) with webhooks; importers for Asana, Trello, Jira, monday.com, Todoist, Wrike and CSV.

The pricing page lists 50+ native integrations including Google Calendar, Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, Jira, Figma, Zapier and Make; Salesforce, Tableau and Azure DevOps are Enterprise only. Public REST API with webhooks on every plan, rate-limited to 100 calls a minute below Enterprise.

Summary

TickTick is a personal planner that puts a task list, a calendar, a habit tracker and a focus timer in one app. It is aimed at individuals who want to schedule their day as well as list what to do.

Tasks live in lists and folders with tags, sub-tasks, checklists and natural-language dates. The same tasks can be shown as a list, a Kanban board, a Premium timeline with durations, a calendar or an Eisenhower matrix, and a Pomodoro timer logs focus time against them. There are no custom fields, dependencies or automation rules, and sharing is limited to small groups on a list.

The free plan stops at 9 lists of 99 tasks, 2 members per shared list and a basic calendar. Premium costs $49.99 a year or $4.99 a month, up from $35.99 and $3.99 in mid-2026, and raises the limits to 299 lists of 999 tasks while adding the timeline, multiple calendar views, task duration and AI features. There is no team tier.

Data is held on AWS in the United States with encryption at rest and no region choice or certifications. The privacy policy says third-party AI providers process inputs but data is not used to train models. A CSV backup and an Open API make leaving possible, but attachments do not come with it.

Portability2.5

Summary

Todoist is a task list for one person or a small team, organised around projects, sections, labels and saved filters. It suits people who want to capture tasks fast and see what is due today, rather than plan multi-step projects.

Tasks carry due dates written in plain language, recurring rules, priorities, sub-tasks and deadlines. Projects can be shown as a list, a board, a calendar or a table, and Business adds shared team projects with roles. There are no custom fields, dependencies, Gantt chart or timer; anything beyond tasks and dates comes from its 130 or so integrations.

The free Beginner plan stops at five projects, three filters and a week of history, with no calendar layout. Pro at $5 a month billed annually lifts those limits to 300 projects and adds reminders, the calendar view and the AI features Task Assist and Email Assist. Business went up in December 2025 to $8 a seat billed annually.

Data is stored on AWS in the United States (Northern Virginia, per the Trust Center FAQ), with no region choice and no self-managed edition; the pricing page lists SOC 2 Type II on every plan, held since late 2025. AI runs through models on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, whose providers have committed not to train on the data. Leaving is workable: the API covers everything, but the in-app CSV export drops comments, labels and attachments, and backups with comments are paid-only.

Assessment

Value for money4.5
A usable free plan with five projects, then $5 a month for Pro and $8 a seat for Business, no seat minimum.
Ease of use4.7
Quick add with natural-language dates means a new user is capturing and scheduling tasks within minutes.
Enterprise features2.0
Business adds roles, central billing and team activity logs, but no documented SAML SSO, SCIM or audit export.
Interface flexibility3.0
List, board, calendar and table layouts with filters and labels, but no custom fields, timeline or built-in automation rules.
Data control3.0
SOC 2 Type II since late 2025 and a GDPR DPA, but all data sits with AWS in the USA, one region.
Portability3.5
Free CSV export per project omits comments; paid backups add comments, and the full API is open on every plan.

2007. Founder Amir Salihefendić launched Todoist as a personal project in 2007; the company behind it formed later.

Todoist Inc. (formerly Doist). Privately held and founder-led, remote-first since 2011 with 108 staff in 38 countries; incorporated in Delaware, USA.

todoist.com

Beginner is free; Pro is $5 per month billed annually or $7 monthly; Business is $8 per user per month billed annually or $10 monthly, raised from $6 and $8 on 10 December 2025.
Free plan
Beginner is free for one person with 5 personal projects, 5 people per project, 3 filters, 5 MB uploads and one week of activity history, but no calendar or table layout and no backups.

AWS in the United States per the security page and privacy policy, which also lists Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud as US-based providers; the Trust Center FAQ names the Northern Virginia region. No EU region choice and no self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security
SOC 2 Type II, listed on the pricing page for every plan and stated in the help centre as of December 2025 (first announced in an October 2025 product update); GDPR compliance with a DPA via the Trust Center; TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest. No SAML SSO or SCIM is documented by Todoist; Business has an admin console with roles and team activity logs.
Calendar sync
Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar on all plans (Outlook was added in June 2025). Time-blocked tasks sync to a dedicated Todoist calendar; changing date, time, title or deleting those events updates the task. Other calendars show read-only inside Todoist. Pro and Business connect up to three calendar accounts.
Data out
Per-project CSV export on all plans (no labels, comments, attachments or reminders); automatic daily backups on paid plans as ZIP of CSVs with up to 500 comments per task and attachment links, 21 kept, completed tasks excluded. Full REST API v1 with backup download and completed-task endpoints.

Web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, Apple Watch and Wear OS, plus browser extensions and email add-ons.
AI
Filter Assist and limited Ramble voice capture on the free plan; Task Assist, Email Assist and unlimited Ramble on Pro and Business. Models run via AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, whose providers have committed not to use the data for training; the privacy policy says Todoist does not train generalised models on user data.
Integrations
The integrations directory lists roughly 134 entries, including Google and Outlook Calendar, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Gmail, Outlook Mail, Zapier, Make, Toggl Track and Jira; a public REST API (v1) with webhooks, an MCP server and a CLI are documented.
Market signal
Todoist’s homepage claims 50+ million professionals, more than 1 million Pro users and 30+ million downloads, and its About page lists 108 staff (both checked November 2026).

Business rose from $6 to $8 a seat (billed annually) for renewals from 10 December 2025; older third-party price lists still quote the earlier figure.

Summary

Wrike is a project management system aimed at organisations that run many concurrent projects, such as marketing departments, agencies and PMOs. Its buyers are usually operations leads standardising how dozens of teams plan, approve and report work.

Work sits in an unlimited folder and project hierarchy, with custom item types, workflows and statuses. Projects can be shown as boards, tables, Gantt charts and calendars, and the higher tiers add workload charts, resource bookings, job roles, budgets, file proofing and approval flows. Setup is the cost: Wrike itself recommends a guided deployment for teams of 20 or more.

The free plan, capped at 200 active tasks, suits a small group trying the board and table views. Team at $10 adds Gantt, calendars and dashboards but is capped at 15 users. Business at $25 brings time tracking, request forms and approvals, needs at least 5 users and annual billing, and seats are sold in groups of five. In January 2026 Wrike retired its Enterprise plan for new buyers in favour of Apex, and from April 2026 AI agents run on monthly action quotas.

Accounts are hosted in Santa Clara, California, or Paris, chosen by where the account is registered. Wrike holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 and 27018, puts SAML SSO and audit reports on Pinnacle, and sells Wrike Lock for customer-managed keys. Its AI addendum says customer data is not used to train models. On Business and above a full account backup exports comments and attachments, but it cannot be restored into Wrike.

Assessment

Value for money2.4
Team at $10 caps out at 15 users; time tracking needs Business at $25 with a 5-seat minimum and annual billing.
Ease of use3.0
Folder, project and workflow configuration is heavy; Wrike recommends a consultant for teams of 20 or more.
Enterprise features4.8
SAML SSO, user audit reports, custom access roles, IP allowlisting and budgeting on Pinnacle; BYOK through Wrike Lock.
Interface flexibility4.5
Board, table, Gantt, calendar, workload, dashboards, custom item types, approvals, proofing and request forms.
Data control4.5
US or EU (Paris) hosting by region, and customer-held encryption keys through the paid Wrike Lock add-on.
Portability3.6
A Business-tier backup includes comments and attachments; the Excel export on every plan drops comments and descriptions.

Wrike-operated data centres in Santa Clara, California (default) and Paris, France; since 5 May 2025 accounts registered from Europe are placed in Paris automatically, and a move goes through the account manager. Summary

Zoho Projects is a project planner for teams that want Gantt scheduling, timesheets and issue tracking at a low per-seat price. It suits small and mid-sized organisations, especially those already using Zoho CRM, Books or Desk.

Work is organised into projects, phases, task lists and tasks, viewed as a classic list, Kanban board, Gantt chart or calendar, with a separate issue tracker for bugs. Blueprints model approval workflows, and Enterprise adds custom profiles, cross-project dependencies, critical path and baselines. Agile sprints live in a separate product, Zoho Sprints.

Pricing is among the lowest here: Premium is $4 a user per month billed annually and Enterprise $9, with no stated seat minimum. The free plan stops at five users and three projects, and time tracking starts on Premium. SSO, webhooks and portfolio dashboards wait for Enterprise.

Zoho runs its own data centres and assigns a region at sign-up, with migration between regions on request. Zia AI runs on Zoho’s in-house model, and Zoho says customer data is not used for training. The portal owner can export a CSV backup once a day, but the help centre does not say whether attachments are included.

Enterprise features3.9

List, Kanban, Gantt and calendar views, custom fields and modules, blueprints, business rules and custom dashboards on Ultimate.
Data control4.2
Region chosen at sign-up from Zoho’s own data centres (US, EU, India, Australia, Japan, Canada and others), with ISO 27001/27701.

Owner-run CSV portal backup, XLSX/CSV module exports, a REST API and importers for MPP, CSV, JSON, Jira and Basecamp.

Coda (Superhuman Docs) - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Not native.

Summary

Superhuman Docs, called Coda until July 2026, is a document in which pages contain linked tables that behave like a database, so a doc can become a task tracker, roadmap or small app. It suits product and operations teams that want to build their own workflow rather than adopt a fixed one.

Any table can be viewed as a grid, Kanban cards, a calendar or a Gantt-style timeline, with formulas, buttons, automations and forms on top. Packs pull Jira, Salesforce or Slack data into tables and push changes back. There is no built-in time tracking, and dependencies that shift dates automatically arrive only on Business.

Billing counts only Doc Makers: Pro is $12 a month billed annually and Business $33, while editors are free. The free plan is generous for small docs but caps shared doc size, attachments and automations. Since the rename, paid plans bundle other Superhuman products, Grammarly on Pro and Mail on Business.

Data is hosted on AWS in the United States with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II; SAML, SCIM and audit logs are Enterprise-only. Third-party AI providers may not train on content, but only Enterprise customers’ AI inputs are excluded from improving Coda’s own AI. Leaving means CSV per table or the API.

Assessment

Value for money4.0
Editors and viewers are free and only Doc Makers pay $12, so a team with a few builders pays little.
Ease of use3.2
A blank doc with tables and formulas, so someone has to build the task tracker before the team can use it.
Enterprise features3.9
SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs and a SOC 2 Type II report, but all only on the quote-based Enterprise plan.
Interface flexibility4.8
Linked tables with any view, formulas, buttons, automations, cross-doc sync, Packs and AI views make almost any workflow buildable.
Data control3.2
ISO 27001/27017/27018, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA, but data is stored only in the United States; BYOK is listed as coming.
Portability3.2
Tables export to CSV and a full REST API is open on all plans, but bulk admin export needs Enterprise.

Free plan

Hosting
Amazon Web Services; Coda states it hosts services and stores data in the US, with cross-regional backups. No residency choice and no self-managed edition.

Summary

GanttPRO is a web-based Gantt chart planner made in Poland, aimed at project managers who want critical path and baselines without Microsoft Project’s weight. Its pages now address construction, manufacturing and consulting teams as well as general project work.

Each project is a task hierarchy on a Gantt chart with dependencies, lags and leads, auto-scheduling, baselines and critical path on every plan. Board, list and dashboard views come with Core; calendar view, custom fields and saved filters start on Advanced; workload, portfolios, budgets and time tracking on Business. There is no rule-based automation, and AI is limited to generating a plan from a prompt, voice note or file.

Core costs $8 per user per month billed annually ($7 from 20 seats), Advanced $12 and Business $19, with monthly billing at $9, $15 and $24 and not offered for a single seat. Enterprise, with SAML SSO, custom roles and unlimited storage, is offered at $25 against a $35 list price, annual only and five seats minimum.

Data is hosted on Microsoft Azure in the EU, under ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and a GDPR DPA; OpenAI is the listed sub-processor for AI plan generation. Exports cover PDF, PNG, XML and Excel, and the API and webhooks give a route out, though comments and attachments have no documented bulk export.

Core is $8 a seat with critical path and baselines, but calendar view needs $12 and time tracking $19.
Ease of use4.3
A Gantt chart with drag-and-drop dependencies and auto-scheduling is usable within minutes; resource calendars take longer.
Enterprise features3.0
SAML SSO and custom roles only on Enterprise, ISO 27001 certified, no SCIM or admin audit log documented.
Interface flexibility3.5
Gantt, board, list, calendar, dashboard, workload and portfolio views, with custom fields from Advanced and no automation.
Data control3.3
ISO 27001:2022 and a GDPR DPA, with Azure hosting inside the EU, but no other region and no self-hosting.
Portability3.3
Projects export to PDF, PNG, XML or Excel and import from MS Project, but only admins can export.
