Hive Work management with many project layouts (Gantt, Kanban, table, calendar, timeline), built-in chat and email, and Buzz AI credits on every plan.
TeamsHive 2015 Medium-large $5Free plan 15-30 3.5Mean of the six criteria: 3.5 out of 5

Hive - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncOne-way: a project can be published as a calendar feed to Google, and connected Google or Outlook events show inside Hive, but edits do not sync back.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. One-way: a project can be published as a calendar feed to Google, and connected Google or Outlook events show inside Hive, but edits do not sync back.

Summary

Hive is a work management tool in which every project can be viewed as a Gantt chart, Kanban board, table, calendar or timeline, with chat, email and meeting notes in the same window. It targets mid-sized teams, especially marketing and agency teams that also want proofing and resourcing.

Projects hold action cards with subactions, custom fields and dependencies; portfolio and summary views roll several projects together. Buzz, the AI assistant, drafts content, summarises work and builds workflows. Much of the depth sits in optional apps: proofing, timesheets, resourcing, dashboards, a CRM and a finance module.

The free plan is usable for small teams, but Gantt, calendar and table views stop after 100 uses each. Starter at $5 caps a workspace at 10 members and 10 projects, so most teams need Teams at $12 billed annually. Each add-on then costs about $5 a user per month, so a team with timesheets, resourcing and SSO pays about $27 a seat.

Hive is SOC 2 certified; its privacy policy places data in the United States, and there is no residency choice. AI requests go to third-party models, and Hive says workspace data is not used to train them. Exports are per view in CSV or Excel; there is no single full-workspace archive.

Assessment

Value for money3.4
A ten-member free plan and a $5 Starter tier, but timesheets, resourcing and SSO each add $5 a user to Teams.
Ease of use3.6
Projects switch freely between familiar layouts, though the many apps, add-ons and AI toggles take an administrator to arrange.
Enterprise features3.4
SAML SSO and Okta SCIM sit in a $5 security add-on, alongside SOC 2 and portfolio views, with no customer-facing audit log.
Interface flexibility4.4
Gantt, Kanban, table, calendar, timeline, matrix and portfolio layouts, custom fields, forms, workflows and dashboards.
Data control2.6
SOC 2 certified with ISO 27001 hosting, but data sits in the United States with no residency choice.
Portability3.4
CSV or Excel export from every layout, MS Project from Gantt, an API and importers for eight tools; comments are not exported.

First launched
2015. Earliest date on Hive’s own timeline: the company graduated from the AngelPad accelerator in 2015. No separate public launch date is given.
Vendor
Hive Technology, Inc. Venture-backed and privately held, based in New York City; raised a $10.6 million Series A led by Comcast Ventures in 2019.
Website
hive.com
Plans
Free ($0, up to 10 members); Starter $5 per user per month billed annually (up to 10 members, 10 projects); Teams $12 billed annually; Enterprise quote-only. Add-ons at $5 per user per month each: proofing, timesheets, resourcing, advanced dashboards, SSO and enterprise security, external users; Finance $12; Hive CRM $29 per seat.
Free plan
Free allows up to 10 members, unlimited tasks and notes, 200 MB of storage and 1,000 AI credits a month, but Gantt, calendar and table layouts are limited to 100 uses each.
Hosting
Multiple geographically separated data centres with ISO 27001-accredited hosting; the privacy policy says data may be stored or processed in the United States and elsewhere. Hive does not name the provider, and offers no data residency choice or self-managed edition.
Security
SOC 2 certified (type not stated on the security page). SAML SSO (Okta, OneLogin, ADFS, Google Workspace, Entra ID), Okta SCIM provisioning, granular permissions and full data erasure in the Enterprise Security add-on at $5 per user per month, included on Enterprise.
Calendar sync
Hive projects can be published as a calendar feed and viewed in Google Calendar; a connected Google or Outlook calendar shows its events inside Hive. Neither direction writes changes back.
Data out
Per-view exports: Gantt to PDF, PNG, MS Project, Excel or CSV; calendar to images, Excel or CSV; table, status and team views to Excel or CSV, with every field except activity. Time and timesheet reports download separately. REST API; guided import from Asana, ClickUp, Jira, monday.com, Notion, Trello, Wrike and Smartsheet, plus CSV, JSON and MS Project.
Platforms
Web; desktop apps for macOS and Windows; iOS and Android apps.
AI
Buzz AI on every plan with monthly credits (1,000 Free, 3,000 Starter, 5,000 Teams, custom on Enterprise) and paid top-up packs; requests are processed by third-party LLMs, and Hive says workspace data is not used to train third-party models.
Integrations
Native connectors include Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Salesforce, QuickBooks, Harvest, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box and OneDrive; the claimed 1,000+ integrations come through Zapier. Public REST API, an MCP server and a Claude connector.
Market signal
Hive’s about page (November 2026) claims more than 2 million people use Hive; its funding record ($1.4 million seed in 2016, $4 million in 2017, $10.6 million Series A in 2019) points to a modest company size.
Caveat
The pricing page shows only yearly-billed prices in its static text; the $18 monthly Teams figure follows from the calculator’s stated saving ($576 a year for eight users), and the monthly Starter price is not shown.

Cycle schedules subscribe as an iCal feed; issue due dates do not sync, and the Google Calendar integration only reads out-of-office events into Linear status.

Summary

Linear tracks issues for product and engineering teams, grouped into teams, short cycles, projects and company-level initiatives. Its reputation rests on speed and restraint, and it is sold to software companies from start-ups to OpenAI-scale customers.

Issues appear in list and board layouts; projects sit on a timeline with milestones and dependencies, and cycles give each team a sprint rhythm. Triage, customer requests and Linear Asks (Slack and email intake) feed work in. What it leaves out is deliberate: no time tracking, no calendar view and no general custom fields. Since 2025 it has added agents, an MCP server and a cloud coding agent.

The free plan admits unlimited members but caps a workspace at 250 issues, so any real team pays. Basic at $10 a seat (yearly) removes the cap; Business at $16 adds private teams, guests, Insights and Asks. SAML, SCIM and the audit log need Enterprise.

Workspaces are hosted in the EU or the US, chosen at creation and fixed, although account and usage data always stay in the US. Linear holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 and offers a HIPAA BAA on Enterprise. Its June 2026 terms state it does not train models on customer data. Leaving means CSV exports without comments, or the API.

Assessment

Value for money3.0
Free seats are unlimited but stop at 250 issues; Basic costs $10 and Insights and private teams need $16 Business.
Ease of use4.5
Opinionated defaults, keyboard commands and fixed issue properties make it usable within an hour, with little to configure.
Enterprise features3.6
SAML, SCIM, audit log, IP restrictions and HIPAA all sit on quote-only Enterprise; Business gets Google SSO only.
Interface flexibility3.0
List, board and project timeline, but no calendar, no general custom fields and dashboards only on Enterprise.
Data control4.0
EU or US hosting chosen at workspace creation on any plan, with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022.
Portability3.5
Issue CSVs omit comments and attachments, but the full GraphQL API is open on every plan and four importers exist.

SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, GDPR, and HIPAA with a BAA on Enterprise only. Google SSO on all plans; SAML, SCIM, IP restrictions, domain claiming and the audit log on Enterprise. Data encrypted with TLS 1.2 in transit and AES-256 at rest.

Summary

MeisterTask is a Kanban task manager from MeisterLabs, the Austrian-German company behind MindMeister. It is sold to small and medium teams, especially in Europe, who want a simple shared board with data kept in Germany.

Projects open as a board or a list; tasks carry checklists, tags, attachments, relationships and a built-in timer whose time slips export to CSV or Harvest. Section automations arrive with Pro. Subtasks, custom fields, roles and a Gantt-style timeline arrive with Business. There is no calendar view, and the Windows and Mac desktop apps were withdrawn in April 2025, leaving web, iOS and Android. Redesigned board, list and timeline views are rolling out in beta during Q4 2026.

The free Basic plan stops at three projects and two integrations. Pro costs €12.50 a seat billed annually, but most teams that outgrow a board will be looking at Business at €24. SAML SSO is held back for Enterprise, priced by quote.

Data sits in Frankfurt on Google Cloud under an ISO 27001 certificate, with a GDPR DPA from a German contracting entity. Meister AI uses Google and OpenAI models that, the vendor says, do not train on customer content; only Business admins can switch it off. Leaving means CSV exports per project plus the public API.

Assessment

Value for money3.0
Three free projects, then €12.50 a seat annually; subtasks, custom fields and the timeline wait for €24 Business.
Ease of use4.5
A clean Kanban board with a per-task timer that a new team understands without training.
Enterprise features3.0
SAML SSO, portfolios and the workload planner are Enterprise only, and no SCIM provisioning is documented.
Interface flexibility3.0
Board, list and timeline views with automations and custom fields, but no calendar view or dashboards.
Data control3.5
ISO 27001 certified with all data on Google Cloud in Frankfurt; EU-only, but no region choice or self-hosting.
Portability3.5

Summary

Motion began as an AI calendar that plans a person’s day by placing tasks into the gaps between meetings. Since 2025 it has been sold to small and mid-sized businesses as a work suite combining projects, docs, meeting notes and AI.

Tasks carry a duration, deadline and priority, and the scheduler rebuilds each calendar as things change. Around that sit projects with list, Kanban and Gantt views, custom fields, dashboards, workflow templates, docs and an AI notetaker. Its 2025 ‘AI Employees’ agents had their own pricing grid from August to November 2025; by November 2026 that page redirects to the homepage.

There is no free plan. Teams pay $19 a seat annually for Pro AI or $29 for Business AI, which adds Gantt, time tracking, capacity planning and permissions; a lone user pays more, from $29. Each seat carries a monthly AI credit allowance, with overage billed per 100 credits.

Data is stored on Google Cloud in Iowa, with no EU option. Motion holds SOC 2 Type II, sends AI requests to OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, and says it never trains models on customer data. There is no export button, so leaving means scripting the API.

Podio - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Not native.
BoardsCard layout groups items by a category field and lets you drag between stages; no WIP limits or sprints.Kanban or Scrum boards: Partial. Card layout groups items by a category field and lets you drag between stages; no WIP limits or sprints.

Podio calendars push to Google, Exchange or iCal one way; external calendars can be overlaid on the personal calendar, but edits there do not flow back.

Summary

Podio is a no-code work platform from Denmark, now owned by Progress Software after it bought ShareFile and Podio in October 2024. It suits small and mid-sized organisations that want to build their own trackers, such as CRMs, project registers or request queues, rather than adopt a fixed task model.

Workspaces hold apps that you design from fields: text, dates, categories, contacts, relationships and calculations. Items appear as tables, cards grouped by category, badges, activity streams or calendars, with comments, tasks and visual reports. Simple workflows arrive with Plus and if-this-then-that automation with Premium; there is no Gantt view and no built-in time tracking.

The free plan is only a trial in practice: five users and 100 items across the organisation. Plus at $11.20 per employee adds unlimited items, external clients and read-only users. Premium at $19.20 adds automation (25,000 actions a month), PDF generation and e-signature; extra API and automation capacity are paid add-ons.

Data is hosted on AWS in Dublin under SOC 2 Type II, with security policies Progress describes as conforming to ISO 27001. An AI Assistant is listed as coming soon on Premium, and an MCP server is in beta. Leaving is laborious: Excel exports omit comments and files, so a full copy needs the API or a backup extension.

Assessment

Value for money2.5
Free stops at 100 items; Plus costs $11.20 per employee and real automation needs $19.20 Premium.
Ease of use2.5
Every workflow begins by designing apps and fields, which suits builders more than people who just want tasks.
Enterprise features2.5
SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001-aligned policies, but SSO only through Google or Microsoft and no SCIM.
Interface flexibility4.0
Custom apps, relationship fields, visual reports and if-this-then-that workflows, though views stop at table, card and calendar.
Data control3.0
SOC 2 Type II with data on AWS in Dublin; one region, no choice offered, and no ISO certificate stated.
Portability2.5
Excel export per app omits comments, files and tasks and stops at 20,000 items; full backup needs the API.

Record

First launched
2011. Official launch in March 2011; founded in Denmark in 2009 as Hoist.
Vendor
Progress Software Corporation. Publicly listed (NASDAQ: PRGS), based in the United States; Podio passed from Citrix (2012) to Cloud Software Group and then to Progress with ShareFile on 31 October 2024.
Website
podio.com
Plans
Free $0 (5 users, 100 items); Plus $11.20 per employee per month annually ($14 monthly); Premium $19.20 annually ($24 monthly). Paid add-ons raise API capacity from $23 a month and automation actions from $39 a month (annual).
Free plan
Free covers up to 5 employees with unlimited workspaces and apps, but caps the whole organisation at 100 items and has no workflows.
Hosting
Amazon Web Services in Dublin, Ireland, with backups in a separate AWS data centre. No region choice and no self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security
SOC 2 Type II (report on request); Progress says Podio conforms to ISO 27001 security policies but does not state a certificate. HTTPS throughout, AES-256 encryption of files. SSO is limited to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 identities, enforced per domain on paid organisations. User management, light users and read-only access on Plus; no SCIM; revision history and activity logs.
Calendar sync
Personal, workspace or app calendars export one way to Google Calendar, Microsoft Exchange or an iCal feed; external calendars can be shown inside the personal Podio calendar, but edits in them are not synced back.
Data out
Excel export per app or view, up to 20,000 items, excluding images, files, tasks, comments and activity; Excel import. Full backups via the REST API or the third-party Backup for Podio extension. API at 1,000 calls an hour, extendable with paid add-ons.
Platforms
Web, iOS (including iPad) and Android.
AI
An AI Assistant (beta) is listed as coming soon for Premium. A beta MCP server with 22 tools lets ChatGPT, Copilot Studio or Claude read and write Podio data. No published statement on training with customer data was found.
Integrations
Built-in links to ShareFile, RightSignature, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, OneDrive and Evernote, Zapier, plus an App Market and third-party extensions such as TimeCamp, Everhour, Globimail and Backup for Podio. Public REST API (1,000 calls an hour, more as a paid add-on), webhooks and a beta MCP server.
Market signal
Progress markets Podio as ‘trusted by thousands of organisations’ and says Progress serves 200,000+ businesses (both November 2026); no Podio user or revenue figure is published.
Caveat
Podio is still sold, now by Progress Software after the October 2024 ShareFile purchase; its AI assistant is still marked ‘coming soon’ on the November 2026 pricing page.
Confidence
High

Summary

ProofHub combines task management with team chat, discussions, notes and a review tool for marking up files and approving them. It is aimed at agencies, creative teams and companies that want one place for internal staff and clients.

Each project offers task lists as boards, a table, a Gantt chart with dependencies and baselines, and a calendar, plus timers and timesheets. Proofing and file versioning are its distinctive parts. There are no automation rules, AI features or dashboards beyond reports, and only seven integrations.

Pricing is flat for the whole account with unlimited users. Essential costs $45 a month billed annually but caps the account at 40 projects and 15 GB, and lacks custom roles, workflows, reports and the API. Ultimate Control is advertised at $89 a month billed annually, but that rate lasts three months before rising to $135. There is no free plan, only a 14-day trial.

The privacy policy says data is held in the United States, and ProofHub publishes no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification and no SSO. Leaving means CSV exports task list by task list, calendar and timesheet downloads, or the API on Ultimate Control.

Assessment

Unlimited users from $45 a month suits big teams, but there is no free plan, and Ultimate Control rises to $135.
Ease of use4.0
Boards, Gantt, chat and proofing sit in one conventional interface that new users and clients follow quickly.
Enterprise features2.0
Custom roles, IP restrictions and activity logs on Ultimate Control, but no SSO, no SCIM and no certifications.

Board, Gantt, table and calendar views, custom fields, forms and workflows, but no automation rules or dashboards beyond reports.
Data control1.5
Data is held in the United States with no named certifications, and the privacy policy still cites the defunct Privacy Shield.
Portability2.6
CSV per task list, iCal or CSV calendars and timesheet exports, but no full account export; the API needs the top plan.

One-way iCalendar feed that Google Calendar and other apps subscribe to, showing tasks on their due dates; MilkSync for Outlook (Pro) syncs Outlook tasks, not calendar events.

Summary

Remember The Milk has been a web to-do list since 2005, run by a small independent team in San Francisco. It suits people who think in tags and saved searches and want reminders to reach them by email or text as well as push.

Everything is a list. Tasks get due dates, priorities, repeats, tags and nested subtasks, mostly typed in one line with Smart Add. Smart Lists are saved searches with almost 50 operators, and MilkScript lets Pro users script changes. There is no board, calendar view, timeline or timer.

The free Basic plan is usable for one person but limits sharing to two others, keeps only a week of completed tasks and leaves out subtasks. Pro costs $49.99 a year and adds Outlook task sync, Zapier, IFTTT, offline web use and the beta AI connector.

Data sits in data centres the vendor does not name, in several locations, and the privacy policy says it is transferred to the United States; there are no certifications. Leaving is straightforward: the account exports to JSON or iCalendar from settings, and a public API with webhooks is open for non-commercial use.

Assessment

Value for money4.5
A free plan with sharing for two people, then Pro at $49.99 a year, about $4 a month.
Ease of use4.0
Smart Add is quick, but getting value from Smart Lists means learning nearly 50 search operators.
Enterprise features1.0
A single-user tool: no team plan, admin console, SSO or audit log.
Interface flexibility2.3
One list view made flexible by tags, saved searches and MilkScript automation on Pro, but no board or calendar.
Data control1.5
Data centres are unnamed and data is transferred to the United States, with no certifications; only encryption in transit is described.
Portability3.5
A self-service JSON export of the whole account plus iCalendar, and a documented API with webhooks, though commercial use needs permission.

Remember The Milk servers in unnamed data centres in several geographic locations; the company is US-based and transfers EEA data under Standard Contractual Clauses. No region choice or self-managed edition.

Taskade - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeA countdown and Pomodoro timer on tasks, with no logged time or time reports.Time tracking: Partial. A countdown and Pomodoro timer on tasks, with no logged time or time reports.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.

Summary

Taskade began as a collaborative outliner and task list and has since rebuilt itself around AI. It suits small teams and solo builders who want shared lists, docs and mind maps alongside AI agents and automations, at a flat workspace price.

Every project is a tree of tasks that can be shown as a list, Kanban board, table, mind map, Gantt chart, calendar, actionsheet or org chart. Tasks take due dates, assignees, custom fields and comments; the timer is a countdown rather than a time log. Since 2025 the product leads with Genesis, which builds small web apps, agents and automations from a prompt.

Free allows two users and no monthly AI credits. Paid plans are flat per workspace: Starter at $6 for three users (annual billing only), Pro at $10 for ten, Business at $25 for unlimited users with SAML SSO. AI credits (10,000 to 400,000 a month) are the real meter, and heavy AI use pushes teams up the tiers.

Data runs in a single AWS US East region. Taskade’s own security page says SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance are in progress and that it offers no signed DPA. Leaving means per-project Markdown or PDF exports or the REST API.

Assessment

Value for money4.5
Flat pricing: $10 a month covers 10 users on Pro, though the free plan has no AI credits.
Ease of use4.0
The outline editor is immediate, but agents, automations and the app builder crowd the interface.
Enterprise features2.5
SAML SSO on Business and SCIM on Enterprise, but SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are still in progress.
Interface flexibility4.5
Eight views over the same tree, custom fields, automations with branching, AI agents and generated apps.
Data control1.5
One AWS US East region, no completed certification and, by its own statement, no signed DPA offered.
Portability2.5
Projects export one at a time as Markdown, text, PDF or image; bulk data out means using the API.

taskade.com

Annual billing saves 50% on Pro and above.

Free covers 2 users, one workspace, one AI agent, 10 automation runs a month and 250MB, with no monthly AI credits.

Teamwork.com Project management for agencies and client-service teams: tasks, Gantt and boards plus time tracking, budgets, invoicing and resource planning.
TeamsTeamwork.com 2007 Medium-large $9.99†Free plan 120-160 3.7Mean of the six criteria: 3.7 out of 5

Teamwork.com - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.

Google and Outlook events flow into My calendar, but editing them back needs Accelerate and tasks are never pushed out to Google or Outlook.

Summary

Teamwork.com manages client projects alongside the money behind them: time logged against tasks, budgets, retainers, invoices and staff capacity. It is sold to agencies, consultancies and other client-service firms that bill for their hours.

Each project offers list, board, Gantt and table views, with dependencies, milestones, subtasks, custom and formula fields, and a site-wide calendar. Clients can be invited into projects and approve files through Proofs. Resource planning, intake forms and invoicing from logged time arrive on Accelerate; quotes, multi-currency budgets and profitability reports need Optimize.

Pricing was restructured in 2026 into Basics at $9.99 and Accelerate at $24.99 per user per month billed annually, with three- and five-seat minimums. Most agencies wanting capacity planning land on Accelerate, at 2.5 times the entry price. AI features are bundled for an introductory period, with usage-based AI credits due to start in late 2026.

Every plan can host data in the US or the EU on AWS, and the company holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; SAML SSO costs extra below Enterprise. The vendor says customer data is never used to train third-party models. Leaving is workable: a full MySQL dump, CSV exports and a public API.

Assessment

Value for money3.0
A five-user free plan, then $9.99 a seat with a three-seat minimum, jumping to $24.99 for automations and capacity planning.
Ease of use3.4
Projects, budgets, rates and resourcing sit side by side, so getting value means configuring the client and financial setup first.
Enterprise features3.8
SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, SAML SSO with auto-provisioning on Enterprise or an add-on, but no documented SCIM.
Interface flexibility4.2
List, board, Gantt, table and calendar views with custom and formula fields, intake forms, automations and dashboards.
Data control4.0
Every plan chooses US or EU hosting on AWS, backed by SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; no BYOK or self-hosting.
Portability3.8
A daily full MySQL backup, CSV exports and a complete API, plus one-click importers from six rival tools.

Record

First launched
2007. Founding year and first release of the project tool (then TeamworkPM) by Peter Coppinger and Dan Mackey in Cork.
Vendor
Teamwork.com (Teamwork Ltd). Headquartered in Cork, Ireland; privately held, bootstrapped for 14 years before a $70 million investment from Bregal Milestone in July 2021.
Website
teamwork.com
Plans
Free ($0, up to 5 users and 5 projects); Basics $9.99 per user per month billed annually (minimum 3 users); Accelerate $24.99 (minimum 5 users); Optimize and Enterprise are quote-only.
Free plan
Free covers up to 5 users and 5 projects with list, board, Gantt and table views, time logging and 100 automations, but only 100 MB of storage.
Hosting
Amazon Web Services in the US or the EU, selectable on every plan including Free; dedicated infrastructure on Enterprise; no self-managed edition.
Security
SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022; two-factor authentication and role-based permissions on all plans; SAML SSO with just-in-time provisioning on Enterprise or the paid Advanced Security add-on; no SCIM documented.
Calendar sync
Google Calendar and Outlook events appear in My calendar on Basics and above; editing those events and logging time from them needs Accelerate. Read-only iCal feeds can be added, and the site calendar can be exported. Tasks are not written to external calendars by the sync.

A full raw MySQL backup of the site can be generated once a day; task, time and report views export to CSV/Excel; REST API with webhooks; importers from Asana, Basecamp, ClickUp, Monday, Trello and Wrike.

Web; iOS and Android apps; desktop apps listed on every plan.
AI
TeamworkAI (summaries, project wizard, AI assistants called Scout, Flo, Remi, Kash and Jack by tier) is included on paid plans for an introductory period before usage-based credits; an MCP server connects Claude, ChatGPT and others. The vendor says data is never used to train third-party models.
Integrations
The vendor claims 150+ integrations, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, HubSpot, QuickBooks and Xero, with Salesforce and NetSuite only on Optimize; there is a public REST API (150 to 500 requests a minute by plan), webhooks and an MCP server.
Market signal
Teamwork reported more than 20,000 customer businesses and 270 staff in its July 2021 funding release; Bregal Milestone’s portfolio page later lists about 300 staff; no newer figures are published.
Caveat
Plans were renamed and repriced in 2026 (Deliver and Grow became Basics and Accelerate), and the pricing page gives both September and November 2026 for the start of paid AI credits.

YouTrack Issue tracker and project tool with agile boards, Gantt charts, timesheets, a knowledge base and helpdesk; sold as Cloud or self-hosted Server.
SoftwareJetBrains 2009 Medium-large $4.50Free plan 100-150 4.2Mean of the six criteria: 4.2 out of 5

YouTrack - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalNo calendar view in the core product; JetBrains publishes a Due Date Calendar dashboard widget, and a full calendar comes from third-party Marketplace apps.Calendar view: Partial. No calendar view in the core product; JetBrains publishes a Due Date Calendar dashboard widget, and a full calendar comes from third-party Marketplace apps.
SyncTwo-way calendar sync: Not native.

Summary

YouTrack is JetBrains’ issue tracker, which has grown into a project tool with a knowledge base and helpdesk attached. It is aimed at software teams first, though JetBrains also sells it to legal, marketing and support teams.

Issues carry custom fields and are driven by commands and a search query language. Agile boards run Scrum or Kanban, an interactive Gantt chart (redesigned in 2026.2) handles dependencies, and timesheets and time reports record logged work. Workflows are scripted in JavaScript. A calendar view is the main gap; it arrives through dashboard widgets or Marketplace apps.

The free tier covers 10 users and 3 helpdesk agents with nothing held back. Since 1 October 2025, Cloud costs $4.50 a seat annually or $5.40 monthly, still among the lowest in this category, and every subscription carries the same feature set.

Cloud instances live in one of four AWS regions (US West, Frankfurt, Ireland, Singapore). The self-hosted Server edition remains on sale, and administrators can download a Cloud database backup and restore it into Server. JetBrains states SOC 2 Type II. AI features route to OpenAI and Google, and JetBrains says AI usage data is not used to train models.

Assessment

Value for money4.6
Ten free users with every feature, then $4.50 a seat annually, with AI, helpdesk and support included in the price.
Ease of use3.0
Commands, a query language and custom workflows reward study; a newcomer meets dense settings before the board feels simple.
Enterprise features3.8
SAML, LDAP and Active Directory login, audit events and granular permissions on every plan, but SCIM is not documented.
Interface flexibility4.6
Agile boards, interactive Gantt, timesheets, knowledge base, helpdesk, whiteboards, dashboards and JavaScript workflows in one licence.
Data control4.7
Cloud in four AWS regions or self-hosted Server, with documented migration between the two in either direction.
Portability4.3
CSV and Excel issue export, a downloadable database backup that restores into Server, a full REST API and over a dozen importers.

Record

First launched
2009. First release of YouTrack in 2009, recorded as a new product that year in JetBrains’ company timeline.
Vendor
JetBrains s.r.o. Privately held and never venture-funded; founded in Prague, Czech Republic, in 2000, the maker of IntelliJ IDEA and Kotlin.
Website
jetbrains.com/youtrack
Plans
Free for up to 10 users; Cloud $4.50 per user per month annually or $5.40 monthly; helpdesk agents beyond 3 at $5.50 annually or $6 monthly; Server free for 10 users, then annual or perpetual user packs from 15 users (shown at EUR 900 a year for 15 users on JetBrains’ European store), with agents at $72 a year.
Free plan
Cloud or Server free for up to 10 users and 3 helpdesk agents with unlimited reporters, with the full feature set, support and AI Assistant included.
Hosting
Cloud on AWS with the region chosen at creation: US West (Northern California), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland) or Asia Pacific (Singapore); moves between regions go through support. YouTrack Server is a self-hosted edition, free for 10 users, with perpetual licences or annual subscriptions above that.
Security
JetBrains states SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance, with report scope listed in its Trust Center; YouTrack Cloud’s inclusion in scope could not be confirmed on a public page. SAML 2.0, LDAP, Active Directory, Okta and other auth modules, two-factor authentication and an audit events log on every plan; SCIM is not documented.
Calendar sync
None native. Due dates can be shown in JetBrains’ Due Date Calendar dashboard widget; Google Calendar sync exists only as a third-party Marketplace app.
Data out
Issue lists export to CSV or XLSX (500 issues by default, raisable by an administrator) including custom fields; articles export to Markdown or PDF. Administrators can download a full database backup and restore it into YouTrack Server. REST API on every plan; importers for Jira, Jira Service Management, GitHub, GitLab, monday.com, Zendesk, ClickUp, Confluence, Asana, Google Sheets, CSV and Excel.
Platforms
Web, YouTrack Mobile for iOS and Android, and YouTrack Server for self-hosting.
AI
AI Assistant on all plans at no extra cost, using weekly free credits: issue and article summaries, alternative titles and comment rephrasing, sent through the JetBrains AI service to providers such as OpenAI and Google, and switchable per group. Built-in grammar and text features run internally. JetBrains says AI usage data is not used to train models that generate code or text.
Integrations
Built-in integrations with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure Repos, TeamCity, Slack and Zendesk, plus about 97 Marketplace apps and 19 dashboard widgets (November 2026); a full REST API, JavaScript workflows and an MCP connection for AI tools.
Market signal
JetBrains reports about 2,800 employees and 3 million customers across all its products (jetbrains.com company timeline, 2024); YouTrack’s own user count is not published, and its Marketplace lists about 97 apps (November 2026).
Caveat
Prices rose on 1 October 2025 for the first time since 2020, and JetBrains lists its SOC 2 scope only in its Trust Center, so YouTrack Cloud’s coverage needs checking there.
Confidence
Medium-high

Akiflow A personal inbox and time-blocking planner that gathers tasks from email, chat and work tools and drags them onto your calendar.
PersonalAkiflow 2020 Medium $19No free plan 15-25 2.1Mean of the six criteria: 2.1 out of 5

Akiflow - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeA focus timer exists, but its sessions are excluded from Stats, which report planned durations only.Time tracking: Partial. A focus timer exists, but its sessions are excluded from Stats, which report planned durations only.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Not native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Not native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncTwo-way calendar sync: Native.

Summary

Akiflow is a planner for individuals who juggle tasks arriving from many places. It collects them into one inbox and asks you to time-block them onto your calendar, and it is sold mainly to founders, executives and other heavy schedulers.

Tasks arrive from Gmail, Slack, Notion, Jira, Asana, Linear and about a dozen other tools, then move to Today, Upcoming or a project, and onto the calendar as blocks. An AI assistant, Aki, answers in the app and on WhatsApp, plans days and reads meeting transcripts. There are no boards, Gantt or custom fields, and team features stop at shared availability.

There is one plan, Pro, at $34 a month monthly or $19 a month on an annual plan the vendor has labelled a promotion for a year. The trial lasts seven days and needs a card, and the AI Meeting Assistant costs $19 a month more. That makes it one of the dearest single-user tools here.

Data sits on Google Cloud in a region the vendor does not name, and Akiflow states it holds no SOC 2 or ISO 27001. There is no export button or public API, and in November 2025 support said backup and export were not on the roadmap. An OAuth MCP server is the only official programmatic route, so leaving is hard. AI features are opt-in, and an addendum says content does not train general-purpose models but may be used to debug and improve Akiflow’s own AI.

Assessment

Value for money1.8
No free plan, a card for the trial, and $34 a month monthly or a promotional $19 annually for one person.
Ease of use3.7
Keyboard-first inbox and drag-to-calendar planning are quick to learn, but connecting and triaging many sources takes setup.
Enterprise features1.2
No certifications, no SSO or admin console; team pricing is by quote but adds little beyond availability sharing.
Interface flexibility2.5
Lists, calendar, projects, tags and an AI assistant, but no board, custom fields or automation rules.
Data control1.8
Google Cloud hosting in an unnamed region and no SOC 2 or ISO 27001, though certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.
Portability1.4
No export feature or public API; support points to a SQLite dump from a debug page, and backups are off the roadmap.

Record

First launched
2020. Year the company was founded and went through Y Combinator (Summer 2020); the vendor publishes no separate launch date.
Vendor
Akiflow Inc., a Delaware corporation with a fully remote team ‘designed in Italy’; Y Combinator lists it in Spain. Privately held, backed by Y Combinator and Benson Oak Ventures.
Website
akiflow.com
Plans
One plan, Pro: $34 a month billed monthly or $228 a year ($19 a month) billed annually; the AI Meeting Assistant is a $19-a-month add-on, and team pricing is by quote.
Free plan
No free plan: a 7-day full-access trial that needs a card and converts to a paid subscription unless cancelled.
Hosting
Google Cloud Platform, region not stated; no region choice and no self-managed edition. The company participates in the EU-US, UK and Swiss-US Data Privacy Frameworks.
Security
TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. The vendor states it holds no SOC 2, ISO 27001 or FERPA certification. No SSO, SCIM or audit log.
Calendar sync
Two-way event sync with Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar and iCloud Calendar on Pro: events can be created, edited and deleted in Akiflow; iCloud sync is periodic.
Data out
No documented export or backup feature; support has pointed users to a SQLite export from a debug settings page. No public REST API; an OAuth 2.1 MCP server can read and write tasks, subtasks and events.
Platforms
Web, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, Apple Watch and Wear OS. No Linux app.
AI
Aki, a chat and voice assistant in the app and on WhatsApp, plus auto-scheduling and AI project assignment, all included in Pro; the AI Meeting Assistant is a $19 monthly add-on. AI features are opt-in under a Privacy Policy Addendum for AI Features: content is not used to train or fine-tune general-purpose models beyond your organisation, but may be processed to debug and improve Akiflow’s AI and to personalise it. No model provider is named, and none appears in the sub-processor list.
Integrations
19 native connectors including Google, Outlook and iCloud calendars, Gmail, Outlook mail, Slack, Teams, Notion, Asana, ClickUp, Jira, Linear, GitHub, Trello, Todoist and Microsoft To Do, plus Zapier and IFTTT. No public REST API; an OAuth MCP server gives AI assistants read-write access.
Market signal
No user or revenue figures are published; Y Combinator lists a team of 18 and the About page shows 12 people (both checked November 2026).
Caveat
The $19 annual rate is labelled a promotion and could revert without notice, though the label has stood since at least November 2025. The AI addendum lets Akiflow use AI inputs to improve its own features, and the model provider is not disclosed.
Confidence
High

Businessmap Kanban-based portfolio and work management: boards, initiatives, OKRs, Gantt-style planning and flow analytics, sold as one plan with a 15-seat entry.

Businessmap - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.

Summary

Businessmap, called Kanbanize until 2023, grew from Kanban boards into a portfolio management platform that links OKRs and initiatives to the cards teams move each day. It is sold mainly to mid-sized and large organisations running Lean or Agile at scale.

Work lives on configurable Kanban boards inside workspaces, with initiatives above them on a Gantt-style planning view that supports predecessor links, critical path and milestones. A calendar shows deadlines, cards carry logged time with worklog reports, and flow metrics such as cycle time and blocked time are built in. Business rules automate moves and updates.

There is one feature-complete Standard plan and no free tier. It starts at 15 seats: $10.60 per user annually ($12.70 monthly), falling with volume. Automation rules and SSO cost extra, and Enterprise adds dedicated hosting and support.

Shared accounts are hosted on AWS in the US or the EU, with dedicated instances in other regions for large customers, and Businessmap states ISO 27001:2022 compliance. AI tools draft subtasks, comments and summaries through Azure OpenAI in Sweden or AWS, and the November 2026 privacy policy says this content is not used to train models. Data leaves through Excel exports and the REST API.

Assessment

Value for money2.2
No free plan, a 15-seat entry at $10.60 a seat, and automation rules and SSO both billed as add-ons.
Ease of use2.6
Workflows, lanes, initiatives and WIP policies assume Kanban knowledge; most rollouts lean on training or the vendor’s consultants.
Enterprise features4.0
SAML and OIDC SSO as an add-on, audit logs, granular roles, ISO 27001:2022 and dedicated infrastructure above 500 users.
Interface flexibility4.6
Boards, portfolio workspaces, Gantt planning view, calendar, OKRs, whiteboards, dashboards, flow analytics and IF-THEN business rules.
Data control4.2
EU (Dublin, Frankfurt) or US hosting on shared plans, with dedicated AWS instances in other regions on request.
Portability3.3
Search results export to Excel and add-ins sync with Excel or Sheets, but there is no full-account JSON export.

Record

First launched
2011. Launched as Kanbanize on 1 January 2011; renamed Businessmap in October 2023.
Vendor
Businessmap (formerly Kanbanize). Privately held and founder-led; offices in Sofia, Bulgaria, Bilbao, Spain and São Paulo, Brazil.
Website
businessmap.io
Plans
Standard (all features) from $10.60 per user per month annually or $12.70 monthly, sold from 15 seats; automation rules and SSO are paid add-ons; Enterprise is quote-only, adding a dedicated cloud instance, IP whitelisting, 1 TB storage and a customer success manager.
Free plan
No free plan; a free trial with full features, including analytics, is offered instead.
Hosting
AWS: US (Virginia) by default for the Americas, Ireland or Frankfurt for EU customers; dedicated infrastructure (optional at 500 to 1,000 users, mandatory above 1,000) can be placed in Germany, Spain, São Paulo, Sydney and other regions on request. No self-managed edition.
Security
ISO 27001:2022 and PCI-DSS compliance stated, twice-yearly third-party audits including penetration tests, TLS 1.2 in transit and AES-256 at rest. SAML and OIDC SSO with Okta, Entra ID or OneLogin as a paid add-on; audit logs and admin roles; IP whitelisting on Enterprise. No SOC 2 report was found.
Calendar sync
None native. The built-in calendar shows card deadlines and other dates inside Businessmap only; sync with external calendars needs Zapier, Make or Power Automate.
Data out
Advanced search results export to Excel with configurable fields, links and subtasks; dashboard widgets export their data; Excel and Google Sheets add-ins import and export cards. REST API (with call limits on Standard) and a remote MCP server. Import is via spreadsheet templates; Enterprise includes free migration from other tools.
Platforms
Web, plus iOS and Android apps listed as “Businessmap formerly Kanbanize” (App Store and Google Play, both last updated in January 2026).
AI
AI Tools generate subtasks, comments, emails and summaries on cards; the AI Coach analyses workflow and card data; whiteboards add AI insights; included in the plan and switchable by an administrator. The privacy policy (updated 6 November 2026) says request content goes to Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service in Sweden or to AWS in the organisation’s data centre, and that neither Businessmap nor its AI providers use it to train models. A remote MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT and other clients query the account.
Integrations
Native integrations listed for Jira, GitLab, Bitbucket, Subversion, Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio, Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, Excel and Google Sheets add-ins, plus Zapier, Make and Power Automate; a REST API and a remote MCP server.
Market signal
Businessmap says it is trusted by 1,000+ enterprise PMO and portfolio teams and lists 300+ partners and offices in three countries (businessmap.io, November 2026); it publishes no user or revenue figures.

Prices come from the vendor’s live pricing calculator, which starts at 15 seats; there is no free plan, and automation rules and SSO add to the per-seat price.

Medium-high

Celoxis Project portfolio management for PMOs: scheduled Gantt plans, resource capacity, timesheets, costing and billing, in the cloud or on-premise.
EnterpriseCeloxis 2001 Medium $10†No free plan 20-30 3.6Mean of the six criteria: 3.6 out of 5

Celoxis - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.
CalCalendar view: Native.
SyncA calendar subscription URL publishes Celoxis events and task dates to Outlook or Google Calendar; nothing comes back.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. A calendar subscription URL publishes Celoxis events and task dates to Outlook or Google Calendar; nothing comes back.

Summary

Celoxis is a project portfolio management system that has been sold since 2001, built in Pune for PMOs that run scheduled projects alongside resource capacity, budgets and billing. Its buyers are manufacturing, technology, healthcare and services firms rather than small teams.

Plans are task hierarchies with all four dependency types, constraints, baselines and critical path. Every report can be shown as a table, Gantt, calendar, card board with draggable lanes or chart, and dashboards are built from those reports. Timesheets with timers and approvals, expenses, risks and issues and custom workflow apps sit beside the projects. Scrum is handled by convention, with sprints as summary tasks, rather than as a dedicated mode.

Core costs $10 per full-access user per month billed annually, with a five-user minimum, and already includes workload tracking and capacity planning; timesheets cost $5 more on Core or come with Essentials at $25, which adds job roles and resource-conflict checks. Project billing, the client portal and an undefined “advanced security” bundle need Business at $45. Enterprise, which includes the on-premise licence, is quoted.

The cloud runs on AWS with a choice of US or Ireland data centres, under ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, and a self-hosted edition runs on PostgreSQL, SQL Server or Oracle. The Lex assistant uses Microsoft Azure AI Services and is not priced separately. Exports are CSV and PDF; the REST API and webhooks are the fuller route out.

Assessment

Value for money2.5
Core is $10 with capacity planning, but a five-seat minimum applies and timesheets add $5 or need Essentials at $25.
Ease of use2.5
A scheduling engine with constraints, work calendars and role-based privileges needs a trained administrator to set up.
Enterprise features4.0
SAML SSO, roles and privileges, activity logs, portfolios and SOC 2 Type II, though no SCIM is documented.
Interface flexibility4.3
Gantt, card, calendar and chart outputs on any report, dashboards, formula fields and custom workflow apps.
Data control4.5
A self-hosted edition on Linux, Windows or macOS, plus a choice of US or EU cloud on AWS.
Portability3.5
Gantt and reports export to CSV and MS Project plans import intact, but there is no full workspace export.

Record

First launched
2001. Launch of the web-based product after two years of development, as Celoxis’s own history records it.
Vendor
Celoxis. Privately held and founder-led (Nikhil Daddikar and Ravindra Wankar); head office in Pune, India.
Website
celoxis.com
Plans
Core $10, Essentials $25, Professional $35 and Business $45 per full-access user per month billed annually, with cheaper team-member and timesheet-only seats from Essentials; Enterprise (including on-premise) is quoted.
Free plan
No free plan; a 14-day trial runs on the Business feature set, and paid plans add free client users plus 2 (Core) to 15 (Business) free read-only users.
Hosting
Celoxis Cloud on AWS in the United States (default) or Ireland (EU), chosen at sign-up. A self-hosted edition runs on Linux, Windows or macOS with PostgreSQL 12+, SQL Server 2016+ or Oracle; on-premise releases follow the cloud by about a month, and moving from cloud to on-premise is charged.
Security
ISO 27001 and AICPA SOC 2 Type II audited; EU and UK GDPR. SAML 2.0 SSO tested with Google, Salesforce, Okta, OneLogin, Azure and ADFS, with no plan stated; an undefined “Advanced security” item is listed only on Business and Enterprise. Two-factor authentication (in beta); role-based privileges; request logging and an activity log report. Encrypted snapshots every 30 minutes. No SCIM or customer-managed keys documented.
Calendar sync
One-way: a calendar subscription URL publishes Celoxis events and task dates to Outlook (Open Calendar, From Internet) or Google Calendar, refreshed on the calendar client’s schedule.
Data out
Gantt plans export to CSV; reports download as CSV (flat or grouped), PDF or image. Imports from MS Project (keeping dependencies and constraints) and CSV for tasks, users, clients and time. REST API reads and writes projects, tasks, time, expenses and custom fields, rate-limited from 150 requests an hour on Core to 1,800 on Enterprise; webhooks. On-premise customers hold the database.
Platforms
Web; iOS and Android apps for task updates, time logging and approvals.
AI
Lex, a natural-language assistant over live account data, not listed as a paid item on the pricing page; Microsoft Azure AI Services is the only listed AI provider. Neither the AI addendum nor the AI providers page says whether customer data trains models. A beta MCP server connects ChatGPT Desktop, Claude Desktop and Cursor.
Integrations
21 integrations are configured inside Celoxis, including two-way Jira and Azure DevOps sync, Salesforce, QuickBooks Online, Slack, Okta and MS Project; Zapier and n8n cover the rest, beside a REST API, webhooks and a beta MCP server.
Market signal
Celoxis reports 500+ active customer organisations and more than one million projects run (celoxis.com, about page, November 2026), and 550+ G2 reviews.
Caveat
The plan line-up (Core to Business) is new enough that third-party comparisons still quote older tiers; and the five-user minimum means the real entry price is $50 a month, billed annually.
Confidence
High

Capabilities

TimeTimesheet entries on cards and timesheet reports are Enterprise only; other plans have estimates and time-on-board only.Time tracking: Partial. Timesheet entries on cards and timesheet reports are Enterprise only; other plans have estimates and time-on-board only.

Summary

Favro is a Swedish planning tool built by the founders of an earlier enterprise agile product. It is sold to teams that run several boards in parallel, especially game studios and software companies, and to managers who need to see across them.

Its distinctive idea is that one card can live on several boards at once, so a task appears on a team’s Kanban board, a manager’s sheet and a roadmap without copying. Collections group boards; backlogs nest cards into hierarchies; relations, dependencies, burndowns, dashboards, forms, documents and a calendar sit on top, and rule-based automations move work along.

There is no free plan. Lite at $5.10 a user is limited to five collections, 25 automation actions a month and no integrations or API, so most teams will need Standard at $6.80. Users are billed in buckets from two seats, and timesheets, SAML SSO and SCIM are Enterprise only.

Data stays in the EU on AWS Frankfurt and Cleura in Sweden, under ISO 27001 and 27701 certificates and a DPA. Favro has no built-in AI and charges no AI fees; an official MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor act on your behalf. Leaving means board-by-board exports or the API on Standard.

Assessment

Value for money3.0
Cheap at $5.10 Lite, but no free plan, 2-user buckets, and Lite drops integrations, the API and reports.
Ease of use3.5
Cards that live on several boards at once are flexible but take a team time to model well.
Enterprise features3.5
Enterprise adds SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, collection management and timesheets; no audit log or portfolio layer is advertised.
Interface flexibility4.5
Boards, sheets, roadmaps, backlogs, calendar, dashboards, documents, forms, relations and 5,000 monthly automations on Standard.
Data control3.5
ISO 27001 and 27701 certified with data held in the EU (Frankfurt and Sweden); no region choice yet.
Portability3.0
Boards export to Excel, CSV or JSON from sheet view, but the API is closed to Lite customers.

Uppsala collaborative technologies AB, trading as Favro. Privately held, registered in Uppsala, Sweden; founded by Hans Dahlström, Erik Olofsson and Patric Palm, whose earlier agile-planning company was sold to a US acquirer.

favro.com
Plans
Lite $5.10 per user per month annually ($6 monthly); Standard $6.80 annually ($8 monthly); Enterprise tailored pricing via sales. Minimum bucket is 2 users.

No free plan; every paid plan has a 14-day trial without a card.
Hosting
EU only: AWS in Frankfurt and Cleura (City Network) in Frankfurt and Sweden, with attachments in AWS S3. No region choice today; Favro says an Enterprise Plus plan will add it. No self-managed edition.
Security
ISO/IEC 27001 and 27701 certified by a third party; PCI DSS SAQ A. TLS 1.2+ in transit, database and backups encrypted at rest. Google and GitHub OAuth on all plans; SAML SSO (Okta, OneLogin) and SCIM 1.0/2.0 on Enterprise. No audit log published.
Calendar sync
Each member can connect Google or Microsoft calendar so start and due dates of cards assigned to them appear there; one way, and only for cards assigned after connecting. A built-in calendar shows dated cards across collections.
Data out
Board export to Excel, CSV or JSON from sheet view; whether comments and attachments are included is not documented. The REST API reads cards, comments, custom fields and dependencies. Importers for Trello, Basecamp Classic and CSV or Excel. API and webhooks on Standard (1,000 calls an hour) and Enterprise (10,000).
Platforms
Web, iOS, Android, and desktop apps for macOS and Windows.
AI

API and webhooks on Standard and Enterprise only; Lite gets only primary integrations.
Market signal
Favro publishes no user, customer or revenue figures (checked November 2026); its site points to game-development, SaaS and enterprise teams, and its App Store listing carries 12 ratings.
Caveat
The year marks the first dated app release found; Favro does not publish a launch date, user numbers or revenue.

Fibery - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeFibery offers time tracking as copyable templates: a lightweight tracker built from fields and action buttons, and a fuller Time Tracker Pro with time-log databases and formulas; there is no native timer or timesheet module.Time tracking: Partial. Fibery offers time tracking as copyable templates: a lightweight tracker built from fields and action buttons, and a fuller Time Tracker Pro with time-log databases and formulas; there is no native timer or timesheet module.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Native.

SyncGoogle Calendar and other calendar accounts sync events into a Fibery database; nothing is written back to the external calendar.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. Google Calendar and other calendar accounts sync events into a Fibery database; nothing is written back to the external calendar.

Summary

Fibery is a configurable workspace in which a team defines its own databases (tasks, features, clients, objectives) and links them, then works on them through views, documents and automations. It suits product teams, agencies and start-ups that want one tool shaped to their process.

Every database can be shown as a board, table, list, timeline with dependencies, Gantt, calendar, gallery, feed or map, with charts and dashboards over the data; whiteboards and collaborative documents link to entities. Rules, buttons and JavaScript scripts automate work. The cost of that freedom is set-up: nothing works until someone designs it, and time tracking is something you build.

The free plan covers 10 users and 10 databases. Standard at $12 a seat (annual) adds unlimited databases, charts and whiteboards; Pro at $20 adds custom apps, advanced permissions, JavaScript automations and shared Gantt views; Enterprise at $40, from 25 seats, brings SAML, SCIM and regional hosting.

Data is hosted on AWS in the EU unless an Enterprise customer chooses the US, UK or APAC, and Fibery holds a SOC 2 Type II report. Its AI terms forbid providers from training on inputs or outputs. Leaving is straightforward: a full Markdown and CSV export on every plan, plus REST and GraphQL APIs.

Assessment

Value for money3.6
Ten free users with real databases, then $12 a seat; SSO needs the $40 Enterprise plan with 25 seats minimum.
Ease of use2.5
A blank workspace means designing databases, relations and views first; Fibery itself calls the people who do this Architects.
Enterprise features3.6
SOC 2 Type II, audit logs and granular sharing, but SAML, SCIM and IP restrictions arrive only on Enterprise.
Interface flexibility4.9
Custom databases and relations, formulas, ten view types, charts, whiteboards, JavaScript automations and AI-built custom apps.
Data control3.8
EU hosting by default with SOC 2 Type II; US, UK or APAC residency only on the Enterprise plan.
Portability4.3
Any plan can export the whole workspace as Markdown and CSV, with REST and GraphQL APIs and CSV import.

2019. Fibery 1.0 opened public registration in November 2019 after a private beta from early 2019.

Fibery Limited. Privately held, venture-funded ($8.3 million to date); founded in 2016 by Targetprocess co-founder Michael Dubakov, remote team with offices in Warsaw and Nicosia.

fibery.com

Free for up to 10 users; Standard $12 per user per month annually ($15 monthly); Pro $20 ($24 monthly); Enterprise $40 ($50 monthly) with a minimum of 25 paid users. AI credits come with each paid seat (250, 500 or 1,000 a month by plan), and Pro and Enterprise can buy extra usage at $15 per 1,000 credits.
Free plan
Up to 10 users and 10 guests with 10 databases, unlimited entities, 1 GB of files, 250 automation runs a month and no AI credits; timeline, Gantt, whiteboard, feed, map, chart and dashboard views are private-only.

AWS (EC2 and RDS). EU data residency on all plans; Enterprise can choose EU, US, UK or APAC. No self-managed or on-premise edition.

SOC 2 Type II report from an independent auditor (on request); GDPR DPA; data encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. Google login on all plans, Microsoft login on paid plans; audit log kept 14 days on Free, 90 days on Standard, unlimited on Pro and Enterprise; SAML SSO, SCIM, IP restrictions and session settings on Enterprise.
Calendar sync
One way into Fibery: the Google Calendar integration syncs meetings, holidays and other events into an Events database shown in calendar views, and Pro and Enterprise can sync several email and calendar accounts per user. Fibery entities are not pushed to external calendars and no iCal feed is documented.
Data out
Export of the entire workspace as Markdown plus CSV on every plan; CSV import with field mapping; REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks via automations, a custom-integration SDK and one-way Fibery-to-Fibery sync.

AI

A remote MCP server on every plan serves Claude, ChatGPT and other agents. Fibery’s AI Terms (October 2026) state it does not use customer data to train third-party foundation models and contractually bars AI providers from training on inputs or outputs.

Built-in synced integrations with 20+ tools including Jira (two-way on Pro and Enterprise), GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Zendesk, Intercom, HubSpot and Google Calendar, plus Zapier and Make; public REST and GraphQL APIs, a custom-integration SDK and an MCP server.

Fibery is a small company (30 staff and 1.6 times as many paid accounts in 2025 as the 530 it had at the end of 2024, short of a 1,000 target). It set itself the goal of profitability in Q3 2026 and has published no update since, which matters for a tool you build your processes inside.

High

Freedcamp - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

Summary

Freedcamp is a long-running, low-cost project workspace from a small Californian company. It suits small businesses, schools and non-profits that want several teams in one place without per-seat bills, and offers discounts to education and non-profit users.

A project bundles separate apps: tasks shown as a list, Kanban board or table, a calendar, milestones, time tracking, discussions, files and a password store. Business adds a Gantt chart with dependencies, critical path and slack time, plus a wiki, issue tracker, CRM, invoices, reports, custom fields and custom statuses. There is no general rules engine for automation; recurring tasks are the main exception.

The free plan has no user or project cap, which is rare. Pro at $1.49 adds table view, subtasks, recurring tasks, Google Calendar push and cloud-file links, but most teams will want Business at $7.49 for the Gantt and custom fields. Guests and read-only collaborators cost nothing.

Data sits on AWS in the US; Freedcamp cites AWS certifications rather than its own and handles EU transfers through the Data Privacy Framework. Leaving relies on per-app XLS exports, which omit comments, or Business backups in XLS and XML with attachments, plus the public API.

Assessment

Value for money4.8
Unlimited free users and projects, then $1.49 Pro; Gantt and custom fields need $7.49 Business.
Ease of use3.8
Each project switches on separate apps (tasks, time, wiki, CRM), which takes some setting up and learning.
Enterprise features2.5
SAML SSO (beta) and white label on Enterprise, but no SCIM, audit log or certifications of its own.
Interface flexibility3.5
List, Kanban, Gantt, calendar and table views with custom fields and statuses; dashboards only on Enterprise.
Data control2.5
Runs on AWS in the US with no own certifications; Enterprise can buy a private instance in a chosen region.
Portability3.0
Per-project XLS exports skip comments; XML backups with files need Business; imports accept XLS tasks only.

First-party links to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Slack, Google Calendar and email-in, plus Zapier for everything else. A public API is on every plan, and a hosted MCP server with 102 tools launched in 2026.

Summary

Nifty gathers a project’s milestones, tasks, documents, files and team chat in one workspace, with each project opening on a roadmap of milestones. It is aimed at agencies, product teams and small companies that work with clients.

Projects combine a Gantt-style milestone roadmap with task lists, Kanban and swimlane boards, and team calendars. Tasks carry custom fields, dependencies, story points and timers. Portfolios, workloads, goals and automatic check-ins roll work up across projects, and clients join as guests. Orbit AI drafts documents and generates projects and tasks.

Pricing comes in two forms: per-member plans (Pro $10, Business $16 billed annually) for small teams, and flat bundles (Pro $79 for 10 members, Business $124 for 30, Unlimited $399) for larger ones. The free plan admits unlimited members but only two active projects. Time tracking and custom fields start on Pro; the API and Microsoft SSO need Business.

Data sits on AWS under SOC 2 and ISO 27001:2022 audits, with no region choice. Orbit AI sends content to OpenAI, which Nifty says may not train on it. Leaving is harder than arriving: importers cover nine tools, but there is no documented workspace export.

Per-member Pro at $10 suits small teams, flat bundles get cheap past seven people, but Free stops at two projects.

Each project opens on a familiar roadmap, task board and discussion, so small teams start quickly without configuration.

Capabilities

TimeManual ‘time needed’ and ‘time spent’ fields with section and project totals, on Premium and above; no timer or time reports.Time tracking: Partial. Manual ‘time needed’ and ‘time spent’ fields with section and project totals, on Premium and above; no timer or time reports.

Summary

Nozbe is a Polish task manager built around task-based communication: discussion happens in comments on tasks rather than in chat or email. It is sold to freelancers and small teams, with industry pages aimed at lawyers, estate agents and agencies.

Work is organised as spaces, projects, sections and tasks, with an Incoming list for anything needing a person’s attention and a Priority list for their own day. A calendar view shows dated tasks, and AI can build a project from a description or a CSV file. There is no board, Gantt or custom field, and time tracking is manual fields only.

The free plan covers three people and three projects. Premium is $9 per user per month (annual) for a single space; Business at $15 adds one subscription across spaces and unlimited admins. Per-user prices fall from ten users.

Servers are at Hetzner in Germany, with backups and files on AWS in Paris and Frankfurt; a GDPR DPA is offered, but no certification or SSO. Nozbe AI uses Gemini; the vendor makes no statement on training. Task lists export to CSV, support will send a ZIP archive of all data, and a documented REST API makes leaving straightforward.

Assessment

Value for money3.6
A free plan for three people and three projects, then $9 a user, falling to $8 at ten users.
Ease of use4.5
Projects, tasks, comments and a Priority list: a new team understands the model within minutes.
Enterprise features1.8
Admin roles and member groups only; no SSO, SCIM, audit log or security certification is documented.
Interface flexibility2.3
List and calendar views with sections, tags and templates, but no board, Gantt or custom fields.
Data control2.5
All data in the EU on Hetzner in Germany and AWS in Paris and Frankfurt, with a DPA but no certification.
Portability3.8
Task lists export to CSV, support sends a ZIP of everything, and the REST API and importers are on every plan.

One space for up to 3 people with 3 active projects, 3 sections, 3 tags, 7 days of completed-task history and 500 MB of storage.
Hosting
Main servers at Hetzner in Germany; encrypted database backups on AWS S3 in Paris; uploaded files on AWS S3 in Frankfurt with backups in Ireland. EU only, with no region choice and no self-managed edition.
Security
TLS in transit, encrypted files and backups, point-in-time restore on request, SMS two-factor sign-in on paid plans; no SSO, SCIM, audit log or certification is documented; GDPR DPA available to download.
Calendar sync
Two-way Google Calendar and Outlook sync on every plan: your dated tasks in active projects appear in a Nozbe sub-calendar, and events added to it become tasks. A one-way iCal feed per space is also offered.
Data out
Project task lists and the calendar export to CSV (visible tasks only); printing to PDF; a ZIP archive of all projects, tasks and attachments on request to support; a REST API with an OpenAPI 3.0 document and outgoing webhooks. Data is quarantined for 30 days after cancellation, then deleted.
Platforms
Web, iOS, iPadOS, Android, macOS and Windows.
AI
Nozbe AI creates projects from a description (powered by Gemini) and turns CSV files into projects (processed on Nozbe servers): 3 requests on Free, 1,000 on Premium, 2,000 on Business. A remote and local MCP server connects Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. No statement on model training.
Integrations
Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Dropbox, OneDrive, Evernote, email-to-task, Zapier and importers for Asana, monday.com, Todoist and Trello, on every plan; a REST API with an OpenAPI document, outgoing webhooks and an MCP server.
Market signal
Nozbe’s press page (read November 2026) says more than 700,000 people have used the Nozbe system; the about page lists 15 full-time staff and 10 contractors.
Caveat
Nozbe raised the prices of both Nozbe and Nozbe Classic from February 2026, after letting customers lock in the old rate until the end of January. The original Nozbe, now Nozbe Classic, still runs for existing users but gets no new features; this record covers the current Nozbe, formerly Nozbe Teams.

High

PersonalThe Omni Group 2008 Medium $8.33No free plan 3-8 2.7Mean of the six criteria: 2.7 out of 5

OmniFocus - summary, assessment and sources

Capabilities

TimeTime tracking: Not native.
BoardsKanban or Scrum boards: Not native.
GanttGantt or dependency timeline: Not native.
CalForecast is a day-by-day list of due, planned and flagged items, not a calendar grid; on the web it shows tasks only.Calendar view: Partial. Forecast is a day-by-day list of due, planned and flagged items, not a calendar grid; on the web it shows tasks only.
SyncThe Apple apps show device calendar events in Forecast, one-way and read-only; tasks are not written to calendars, and the web app has no calendar integration.Two-way calendar sync: Partial. The Apple apps show device calendar events in Forecast, one-way and read-only; tasks are not written to calendars, and the web app has no calendar integration.

Summary

OmniFocus is the Omni Group’s task manager for people who run their lives by David Allen’s Getting Things Done. It is built for Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Vision Pro, and since 2019 the same database can also be reached from any browser.

Actions sit in projects and folders, carry tags, due, planned and defer dates, and can be sequential so only the next step shows. Custom perspectives filter the whole database, and a weekly review keeps it current. There are no boards, calendar grid, Gantt, time tracking or sharing. OmniFocus for the Web is a companion: you must set up the database in an Apple app first, and it lacks the review, notifications and repeat editing.

There is no free plan. The $99.99 annual subscription includes the Pro apps and web access. Owners of a $74.99 or $149.99 perpetual licence pay $49.99 a year more for the browser. For someone without an Apple device the web app is not usable on its own.

Sync uses end-to-end encryption with a passphrase you choose, and the Apple apps can sync through your own WebDAV server instead of Omni’s, though the web app cannot. There are no published certifications. The Apple apps export CSV, HTML and plain text; AI is limited to on-device Apple Intelligence date parsing and Siri in beta.

Assessment

Value for money3.0
No free plan; $99.99 a year covers every Apple device and the web, or $49.99 a year on top of a licence.
Ease of use2.6
Defer dates, sequential projects and perspectives reward GTD practitioners but take weeks to learn; web setup needs an Apple device.
Enterprise features1.0
A single-user tool: no shared projects, admin console, SSO or certifications; business purchasing is just volume licensing.
Interface flexibility2.8
Custom perspectives and Omni Automation scripting go deep, but every view is an outline, and the web lacks review and repeats.
Data control3.6
End-to-end encryption with your own passphrase and optional self-hosted WebDAV sync, though the web app requires Omni’s sync server.
Portability3.0
CSV, HTML and plain-text exports plus automatic backups in the Apple apps; no REST API and no export from the web.

Record

First launched
2008. OmniFocus 1.0 for Mac, released 8 January 2008; OmniFocus for the Web followed in 2019 as a companion to the Apple apps.
Vendor
The Omni Group, Seattle, Washington, US. Employee-owned and private; founded in the early 1990s as a NeXT consultancy.

omnigroup.com/omnifocus
Plans
OmniFocus Subscription $99.99 a year from Omni’s store (Pro apps plus web); perpetual v4 licences at $74.99 Standard or $149.99 Pro, with web access an extra $49.99 a year or $4.99 a month. Since 2025 the App Store sells new buyers perpetual licences only.
Free plan
No free plan: a 14-day trial of the apps, and a two-week web trial that starts on first login.
Hosting
Omni Sync Server (US-based vendor; region not published) holds an end-to-end encrypted copy. The Apple apps can instead sync via any WebDAV server you run, or stay local only; OmniFocus for the Web requires Omni’s sync server.
Security
End-to-end sync encryption with a user-chosen passphrase; app lock on iOS; no advertising or social-media trackers. No SOC 2 or ISO 27001 claimed. No SSO, SCIM or audit log.
Calendar sync
One-way: the Apple apps display device calendar events alongside tasks in Forecast. Tasks are not pushed to calendars, and calendar integration is not available in OmniFocus for the Web.
Data out
The Apple apps export to CSV, HTML and plain text, keep automatic backups and allow database migration; Omni Automation (Pro) and AppleScript (Mac) script the data on device. No REST API. The web app can view and download attachments but has no export.
Platforms
macOS, iOS, iPadOS, watchOS and visionOS apps, plus OmniFocus for the Web in a desktop browser (designed for computers rather than phones). No native Windows, Linux or Android apps.
AI
On-device only: optional Apple Intelligence date parsing (beta) and Siri AI reminder integration (beta) in OmniFocus 4.9, September 2026; neither runs in the web app. Omni’s privacy page says customer data is not shared with advertising or social-media services.
Integrations
Apple-platform hooks: Siri (Siri AI beta in 2026), Shortcuts, Share Sheet, Apple Reminders capture, Mail Drop email capture and Omni Automation JavaScript plug-ins (Pro). No REST API, webhooks or Zapier connector; the web app has no integrations.
Market signal
No user or revenue figures are published; the About page lists 28 staff (November 2026), and OmniFocus has been a fixture of Apple-platform GTD since 2008.
Caveat
OmniFocus for the Web is not a standalone product: it needs a database first set up in an Apple app, and it lacks review, notifications and repeat editing.

Summary

Paymo began in 2007 inside a small web agency as a way to see where billable hours went, and it is still built around that loop: track time on tasks, then invoice the client. It suits freelancers and agencies of up to a few dozen people.

Projects hold task lists with list, table, calendar and Kanban views, plus a meta-Kanban board across projects. Time comes from in-app timers, desktop and mobile apps or the automatic Paymo Track, and feeds timesheets, estimates, invoices, expenses and profitability reports. Pro adds Gantt charts with dependencies, a portfolio Gantt, team scheduling with workload, timesheet approvals and leave planning. There is no AI and no workflow automation.

The free plan is for one person with one client and two projects. Solo costs $5.90 a month billed annually for one user; teams need Plus at $10.90 per user billed annually ($15.90 monthly), which also unlocks integrations and the API, or Pro at $16.90 for scheduling and Gantt.

Data is hosted on Amazon Web Services; Paymo publishes no certifications or region and offers no SAML SSO, though two-factor authentication and Google or Apple sign-in are available. The open REST API, with webhooks, covers all account data including comments and files, which makes a scripted exit realistic, while in-app exports are per report or table.

A free single-user plan with invoicing and $10.90 a seat for teams, though Gantt and scheduling cost $16.90.
Ease of use4.0
Timers, task lists and invoices are quick to pick up; scheduling and workload on Pro take more setting up.
Enterprise features1.8
No SAML SSO, certifications or audit log; administration is user roles, guest access, optional 2FA and Google or Apple sign-in.
Interface flexibility3.5
List, table, calendar, Kanban and meta-Kanban views, with Gantt, workload and scheduling only on Pro; no automation.
Data control2.0
An EU company hosting on AWS with a DPO and GDPR commitments, but no certifications and no stated region.
Portability3.5
The REST API reaches all account data, including comments and files, but there is no one-click account export.

Summary

Plaky is a board-based work tracker from CAKE.com, the company behind the Clockify time tracker. It is aimed at small and mid-sized teams wanting a cheap, monday.com-style tool, and is free for any number of users.

Each board is a table of items with typed fields, viewable as a table, Kanban board, Gantt chart or pie and bar charts, with dashboards across boards and rule-based automations. The Gantt shows bars and subitems but no documented dependencies, and there is no calendar view or calendar sync. Time tracking works only by connecting a Clockify workspace.

The free plan has no user cap but limits boards to 6 fields and keeps a 7-day activity log. Pro at $3.99 per seat (annual) adds Gantt, unlimited fields, private boards and 1,000 automation actions a month; Enterprise at $8.99 adds SSO, board permissions and an unlimited log. The $12.99 CAKE.com Bundle includes Clockify and Pumble.

CAKE.com states ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II at company level without naming the products covered, and says most processing is in the United States, with AWS, Microsoft and Hetzner as subprocessors; no Plaky data-region choice is documented. No AI features are listed. Leaving means per-board CSV exports, which omit comments, or the public API released in January 2026.

Assessment

Free for unlimited users, then $3.99 a seat with no minimum; Enterprise with SSO is still under $9.
Ease of use4.3
Spreadsheet-like boards with status columns that a new team can fill in within minutes.
Enterprise features3.1
SSO, board ownership and protected views on Enterprise at $8.99; CAKE.com’s ISO 27001 and SOC 2 name no products in scope; no SCIM.
Interface flexibility3.3
Table, Kanban, Gantt and chart views with dashboards and automations, but no calendar view and a 6-field free cap.
Data control3.0
Company-level ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II without a stated Plaky scope, processing in the USA and no region choice.
Portability3.0
Boards export to CSV without comments, CSV import exists, and an API reaches items and comments on every plan.
